It now resolves to nothing, which is the right outcome — command-not-found beats a wrapper exiting 127 into a discarded stderr, and mover needs root anyway. A /usr/local/bin/mover -> /usr/local/sbin/mover symlink was considered and rejected (supervisor concurred): it puts a file back into the directory this task exists to clear, it lives on tmpfs so it would vanish at the next reboot and mislead anyone comparing boot states, and it exceeds "removal of dead residue only".

4. HEALTHY MOVER INTACT AND FUNCTIONAL, NEVER TOUCHED. /usr/local/sbin/mover 4487 bytes, md5 462e9f2cdbff66f6dd5c9188fc205d4c — byte-identical to the copy inside the squashfs. /usr/libexec/unraid/move present, 31152 bytes; `move -h` prints usage and exits 0. `mover status` exits 1, correct: that branch is literally `[ -f $PIDFILE ]` and no mover is running. Cron entry unchanged: `0 0 * * * /usr/local/sbin/mover start > /dev/null 2> >(logger -t move)`. No cache or share settings touched, and no user data read — this task never went near Pictures, Movies or either consolidate-review copy.

5. PERSISTENCE STATED PLAINLY AND HONESTLY. The box was NOT rebooted, and I am not claiming an observed reboot. What I am claiming is stronger than a single clean boot would have been: there is no code path that could write the file. The upper layer is tmpfs so it cannot persist; the squashfs has no such file so it cannot reappear from the base image; and the flash holds neither the wrapper's text nor any installer that writes that path. A reboot would show the file absent without explaining why; this shows why. The user can confirm at their convenience — a single boot would corroborate, not establish.

ROOT CAUSE IS AN UPSTREAM PLUGIN BUG, not a botched local uninstall. The .plg's install script writes BOTH /usr/local/sbin/mover and /usr/local/bin/mover; its Method="remove" block only does `mv /usr/local/sbin/mover.old /usr/local/sbin/mover` and never touches bin. Install writes two files, uninstall cleans one. Anyone who uninstalls ca.mover.tuning gets the same orphan. Recorded in CAS memory 2026-07-06-2, along with the /usr overlayfs mechanic (check the squashfs lower layer before deleting anything under /usr, or a whiteout may hide a stock file) and the generalised cache rule.

- It is NOT a silent no-op. Run as pippenz it prints "No such file or directory" and exits 127. It only looks silent because callers discard stderr — the cron line does exactly that. The danger is real but the detection story is different, which matters for spotting a recurrence.
- The exposure was inverted from the assumption. Root was never at risk, because its PATH puts /usr/local/sbin first. An interactive pippenz shell was worse off than stated, because the broken wrapper was the ONLY mover on that PATH.

close_reason:
Re-closing after supervisor merge 656cb43. All three hypotheses tested independently, cheapest first; two refuted, one confirmed as a mechanism but refuted as the cause of the stall the user actually complains about. Write-up in docs/a1111-stall-amplifier.md; raw data in /mnt/datacube/staging/cas-00d4/.

H1 CHECKPOINT SWITCH THRASH — REFUTED. Measured switch cost, 8 samples: 3.43-7.28s, e.g. "Weights loaded in 6.2s (calculate hash 2.1s, load weights from disk 0.3s, apply weights to model 3.0s, load VAE 0.2s, move model to device 0.6s)". The historical 141.7s "move model to device" is ~240x today's device phase — pathological, not the normal price. Mechanism also gone: viv-gen.py/shiri-gen.py are deleted and the live a1111 MCP server posts generate_image straight to /sdapi/v1/txt2img with no sd_model_checkpoint and no override_settings, so nothing forces a switch per run. Side finding feeding H3: each distinct checkpoint load leaves ~5 GiB of mmapped page cache in the cgroup.

H2 NTFS/FUSE MODEL STORAGE — REFUTED, premise wrong twice. /mnt/datacube uses the IN-KERNEL ntfs3 driver, not ntfs-3g/FUSE (no ntfs-3g process exists), on /dev/nvme2n1p1 = Samsung 980 PRO 2TB Gen4 — a NEWER, FASTER drive than the 970 EVO Gen3 holding root. Cold sequential read of the 6.46 GiB active checkpoint, 3 passes, per-file posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) rather than global drop_caches so other agents' builds on this shared box were neither perturbed nor allowed to pollute the numbers: ntfs3 median 2862.7 MiB/s (2.31s whole file) vs ext4 median 3181.7 MiB/s (2.03s). 11% gap, 0.28s absolute — worthless against a 141.7s anomaly. Temporary local copy verified byte-identical with cmp then deleted; original only ever read.

H3 MemoryHigh THROTTLING — CONFIRMED as a mechanism, REFUTED as the cause. Reproduced deterministically: from 20.60 GiB, three distinct checkpoint switches drove the cgroup to exactly 32.00 GiB (= MemoryHigh) and memory.events `high` went 0 -> 644, then ~840 per further switch to 4057, while anon stayed FLAT at 6.5-6.7 GiB and file grew 8.1 -> 24.5 GiB. MemoryHigh is firing on reclaimable mmap cache, not on a leak — the opposite of the unit comment's intent. Journal corroborates 4 real sessions at/above 32G, two pinned at EXACTLY 32G with 10.8G/4.3G swap peaks. BUT the 277.4s stall session (2026-07-27T11:25:10) peaked at 10.3G RAM — nowhere near the ceiling — with a 15.9G swap peak (the entire 16 GiB device), and the two sessions either side show identical saturation. Host-wide exhaustion, not cgroup throttling.

CHANGE APPLIED AND SUPERVISOR-APPROVED TO STAY: MemoryHigh=infinity, MemoryMax=44G retained. Before/after over the same 6-switch sequence: throttle events ~840 per switch -> ZERO new; switch wall-time median 4.43s -> 3.74s; cgroup swap flat 1.48-1.51 GiB (peak 1.57 -> 1.71 GiB); host MemAvailable 37.9 -> 42.5 GiB. Reference generations 6.749/6.614/6.648s at torch peak 8517.02 MiB, output PIXEL-IDENTICAL to the cas-2949 baseline. Number justified: MemoryHigh cannot distinguish a leak from reclaimable page cache, so any finite value merely relocates the false positive; MemoryMax is the genuine backstop, reclaiming first and OOM-killing only when it cannot, leaving 18G for the desktop on a 62G box. Revert is one command (systemctl --user set-property a1111 MemoryHigh=32G); prior drop-in backed up at /mnt/datacube/staging/cas-00d4/50-MemoryHigh.conf.backup.

HONESTY ON MAGNITUDE: even while throttled 3184 times, switches cost only ~4s and generations were unaffected (6.825/6.638/6.689s over the limit). Real but cheap today because the over-limit memory is clean cache and the host had 36-42 GiB free; it bites when that memory is anonymous (medvram) or the host is tight. A latent amplifier worth removing, not the smoking gun.

ZSWAP FINDING (cross-filed by the supervisor to cas-d9d6): zswap is enabled (zstd, 20% pool). 2,446,066 pages (9.33 GiB logical) sit compressed in a 2.75 GiB pool with only 688,454 pages (2.63 GiB) ever written back to disk, and the a1111 cgroup reports pswpin 0 / pswpout 0. systemd's "memory swap peak" counts zswap-backed pages, so historical figures like "15.9G memory swap peak" substantially OVERSTATE disk I/O — nobody should read cas-b0b4's telemetry as disk traffic without checking zswap first.

Merged into the epic via 64d07109 (factory/watchful-wolf-66 @ b2f205b5).

WHAT SHIPPED
- New apps/frontend/app/src/utils/api-error-message.ts, framework-free so the message rules unit-test without mounting Vue/Quasar. extractServerMessage reads the response BODY only (data.message / response.data.message). ofetch's FetchError.message is the transport summary `[POST] "http://host/api/v1/orders/service": 400 Bad Request` — it leaks the internal API URL and tells the user nothing — so it is never a source. Handles both server shapes: plain string from `new BadRequestException(...)` and the string[] Nest's ValidationPipe emits (joined with ", "). Capped at 300 chars. isClientError gates to 4xx so 5xx stays behind the generic translation.
- notifyError gained an optional third arg { preferServerMessage }. When set and the status is 4xx it shows the server message (6s instead of 3s, since it carries specifics worth reading); otherwise unchanged. i18n fallback preserved for anything the server did not explain — network failure, 5xx, empty body.
- OrdersServiceOrderDialog's create-order catch opts in, so "One or more product not found: <ids>" (cas-46e3) finally reaches the user.
- Verified end to end that data.message survives the backend HttpExceptionFilter: it writes `error: <msg>` first, then spreads the exception response, so `error` ends up "Bad Request" and `message` holds the real text.

SCOPE DECISION (accepted by supervisor): opt-in per call site, NOT global. For global — notifyError already prefers the server message on 403 and 429, so 400, the status most likely to carry something actionable, is the odd one out, and 86 call sites share the defect. Against — the backend throws 314 BadRequestExceptions and a minority interpolate raw internal error text (`Failed to get combined flags: ${error.message}`, `Invalid storage context: ${context}`, `Failed to fix payment ${id}: ${errorMessage}`), so a blanket flip would put internal failure strings in front of users on unaudited paths; the task text also says to check with Daniel first. Off by default = zero behaviour change at the other 85 call sites. The global flip is now a Daniel decision item with this audit note attached; promoting it is a one-line default change.

Reproduced with an inert performance-only knob so the leak was demonstrated without re-breaking anything: ten brand-new connections inherited a value from a session that had already ended.

CORRECTED PRACTICE, now in the runbook and the residual-execution pack: never SET default_transaction_read_only or SESSION CHARACTERISTICS on pooled; use per-transaction BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY, which cannot leak — the phase3 runners already did this correctly and only the narrative was wrong. Keep writes on unpooled because a transaction pooler is the wrong substrate for multi-statement SERIALIZABLE work, NOT because pooled refuses; it does not refuse, it takes the write. THE DEFECT: the cas-ed15 pull leak (fixed v2.15.0) left every project DB on a multi-project machine carrying other projects' task rows, and nothing in cas ever detected or reported it. Frozen replicas of months-finished work read as `open`, so `task ready` lists another project's backlog as this project's outstanding work. Confirmed present on this machine before writing any code: cas-src's DB shares (id,title) with 130 rows in ozer, 128 in Richards LLC/Accounting, 95 in gabber-studio.

AC1 MET — non-destructive check + named remediation. New `cross-project rows` row in `cas doctor`, plus `cas doctor --foreign-rows` for the full listing (text and --json). Nothing is ever deleted; the message names `cas cloud purge-foreign --dry-run` as the remediation path and restates the identity constraint. Read-only by construction: every database, including the local one, is opened SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY WITHOUT CREATE (so a missing file errors instead of being created as an empty DB that would report itself clean) with a 250ms busy timeout so a live daemon is never blocked.

AC2 MET — identity is (id, trimmed title), never id alone, with the collision regression test. Peer rows sharing an id but not a title are never treated as replicas; they are reported in their own section precisely to warn a human off `DELETE ... WHERE id IN (...)`. id_collision_is_never_reported_as_a_foreign_row_cas_fc6fa builds the measured trap — same id, different real task, and the peer even holds activity evidence for it, so the tempting "id + peer worked it" rule would delete live local work — and asserts the row is a collision, not a foreign row. mixed_id_is_attributed_on_title_and_still_reports_the_collision_cas_fc6fa covers the mixed case (real replica in one peer, unrelated same-id task in another). Trimming is pinned so a stray newline cannot masquerade as a collision.

AC3 MET — closed vs non-closed are counted and rendered separately at every level (summary line, detail listing, JSON), because the non-closed rows are the ones actively lying in ready queues. closed_and_non_closed_foreign_rows_are_counted_separately_cas_fc6fa.

HOW "FOREIGN" IS DECIDED (the part GH #133 left open). Local task rows carry no project column, so attribution uses LOCAL-ACTIVITY EVIDENCE: task_leases, task_lease_history, verifications, verification_dispatches, worker_completion_receipts, worktrees, spawn_queue, loops, worker_delivery_transactions. None of those tables is in the cloud sync payload (entries/tasks/rules/skills/specs/events/prompts/file_changes/commit_links), so a pulled replica arrives without any of them. Verified empirically before relying on it: 1071/1484 cas-src rows carry such evidence, ZERO of the 130 rows shared with ozer do, and 75 of the 128 shared with Accounting have Accounting-side evidence. The evidence is asymmetric — its presence proves nativeness, its absence proves nothing — so a row is called foreign ONLY when this DB has no evidence for it and some peer DB does. Replicas with no evidence anywhere are reported as unattributed ("home unknown"), never accused; rows worked here are native even when peers also hold them (318 of those here).

DELIBERATELY REJECTED: the dependency-orphan fingerprint. A genuine standalone task is a dependency orphan too, so for a REPORT it manufactures false positives on exactly the rows that matter. (It is sound in cas-156b's start advisory only because four further vetoes back it.)

FAIL-CLOSED OUTPUT — no absence-of-warning can be manufactured by an error. A peer DB that exists but will not open is collected with project, path and error, named in the output, and downgrades the row to Warning even when everything readable was clean. task_title: clear_context performs a real context reset for Claude workers — or fails loudly with a verifiable post-condition (GH #145)

clear_context now performs a real, verified context reset for Claude workers, or fails loudly. Merged: factory/rapid-dragon-50 tip 37a91423 landed on epic/github-issue-burn-down-v7-factory-ergonomics-gate--cas-7535 as 2a0c63e6.

ROOT CAUSE: the tool enqueued the literal text "/clear" as an ordinary prompt_queue message; for a Claude worker under Agent Teams that row routes to the team inbox, so the worker read the STRING "/clear" as a teammate note, acknowledged it, and kept its whole conversation — while the tool reported "Queued". Verified live against claude 2.1.224 on a real PTY BEFORE designing anything: typing /clear + CR executes the real slash command, and Claude Code answers by starting a NEW session whose transcript head carries a literal `<command-name>/clear</command-name>` record. That measurement drives the whole design.

FIX: the reset is now a CONTROL command with its own sentinel payload (never readable text) which the daemon matches ahead of all message routing and delivers by typing the recipient harness's own reset command over the interrupt-and-inject PTY channel — it can no longer reach an inbox. clear_context pre-flights every recipient (Codex/Grok are refused up front with nothing queued, because no in-place reset command has been MEASURED for them), waits for the post-condition, and returns old→new session ids plus the evidence path. Unconfirmed, unsupported, or unlocatable ⇒ McpError naming exactly what was and was not observed. AC4: a confirmed reset records the new session id on agent.cc_session_id — the exact key worker_status/worker_activity/is-wedged resolve transcripts by — so the session signature changes and the context band recomputes from the new transcript; the agent-register upsert now COALESCEs cc_session_id so a re-registration cannot erase it.

task_title: Orphaned `cas serve` processes outlive their dead harness session and hold write-side fds on the project cas.db indefinitely
close_reason: `cas serve` now reaps itself when the harness that spawned it dies. The stated hypothesis was falsified before any code was written (a piped-stdin serve whose parent is SIGKILLed exits in 6s — EOF is handled; the leak needs a topology where the stdin write end outlives the harness, e.g. a pty or a sibling that inherited the pipe), so the fix rests on parenthood: new cas-cli/src/mcp/server/parent_watchdog.rs trips only when the ppid has changed since startup AND the new parent is init-like (orphan_gc's systemd --user-aware classifier), confirmed on two consecutive polls; 15s to detect, 10s grace, then hard exit. Armed before eager store init and wired into runtime.rs as a tokio::select! arm beside rmcp's waiting(), so the existing release-tasks/daemon-shutdown path still runs. AC4: orphan_gc could not have fired — its only candidate classes are a worktree cwd and the server_start registry, a main-checkout serve is in neither, and it is a manual force-gated operator action; no second reaper was added. AC5 is structural: each process evaluates only its own parent and exits only itself. Proof: 5 unit tests + 2 integration tests (FIFO stdin held open by the test so EOF cannot fire; bystander-project case), plus full serialized cargo test --no-fail-fast green across 127 binaries. Zero lines in mcp/socket.rs or mcp/daemon.rs (daemon-role half = cas-eabe/GH #163). Merged to origin/main as 7851ea05.

Q3 — contamination enters in exactly one place and it is a CLIENT filter gap, not a server response defect on today's server. knowledge.rs:228 resolves the project id and discards it (`let (url, _project_id) =`); the apply loop :257-273 makes zero entity_matches_project calls; the identifier appears nowhere in the file. project_canonical_id is populated on push (:87) and never read on pull. commit_ingest then merges on rel_path, so a foreign page overwrites a same-named local one unless locked and is unattributable afterwards. TWO NEW BUGS found, neither previously recorded:
(a) The knowledge PUSH watermark advances past server-REFUSED pages. push_knowledge_pages discards the PushResponse (knowledge.rs:196) then sets the watermark to now (:197-199), so a page refused under the locked guard is never retried — it cannot re-enter the `updated_at > since` window (:172-176) until a human edits it again. (b) embed_pending_pages sends every fetched page in ONE embed_batch call (embeddings.rs:490-503) with no internal chunking against a hard server cap of 32. The invariant is held by a duplicated literal 32 at the single call site (cli/cloud.rs:1171) while DEFAULT_EMBED_BATCH=32 sits unused in a different file (embeddings.rs:62). A future caller passing 64 gets a permanent 400 and zero pages ever embedded — silently, since the error is swallowed as a tracing::warn! at cli/cloud.rs:1177.

task_title: Acked messages redelivered via agent-teams channel: two transports, one ack — make ack terminal across both (GH #176)

Traced and fixed GH #176; commit a71de1df now merged into epic/github-issue-burn-down-v8-delivery-state-machine-m-cas-2627 (verified via git branch -r --contains).

Mechanism was NOT the stated hypothesis. The duplicated resource is the read LEDGER, not the message copy, and the re-injector is CAS's own inbox_poll rather than the agent-teams harness. poll_unseen_for_recipient defines "unread" as "no prompt_queue_recipient_seen row" (prompt_queue_store.rs:1991-2000), but the only writers of that table were CAS's two surfacing paths (:3739-3745); the transport that actually delivers to a Claude teammate (agent-teams inbox file via write_to_inbox, delivery.rs:424-456, or a PTY injection) recorded delivery only in prompt_queue columns — mark_transport_delivered (:3201-3218) stamps stage/processed_at and writes no receipt. Even DeferredInboxOutcome::HarnessConsumed (queue_and_events.rs:2288), CAS's strongest surfacing evidence, left the ledger empty. So a row could be `delivered` per message_status and unread per the recipient's own poll at the same instant.

Proven against the live DB, per the binding handoff method (join redelivered rows to their receipts before touching the transport): zealous-fox-95's 8210/8215/8217 and nimble-gazelle-41's 8221/8223/8225/8229/8241 each have their entire receipt set stamped at ONE instant with source='inbox_poll', 14-18 minutes after transport delivery. The acks (inferred_from_reply) landed AFTER the redelivery; 8221/8223 had no ack and no receipt at all for the whole interval. So "acked then redelivered" is not what happened — the poll created the first receipt those rows ever had.

Fix: new PromptQueueStore::record_recipient_surfaced + SurfacingSource::TransportDelivered, written at the three points where the daemon declares a row terminally delivered to a named recipient (HarnessConsumed arm, single-target success arm, broadcast fan-out success arm), keyed on the addressed target so the supervisor's supervisor/pane alias split cannot strand a row. Broadcasts matter most: all_workers is exempt from every row-level ack filter, so the receipt table is the only thing that can retire one for a worker that already received it. Deliberately unchanged and documented as decisions in code: cas-ac7e's explicit-ack-only filter (GH #130 reasoning intact) and the cas-45c4 ack ladder — the receipt sets no acked_at, since delivery is not acknowledgment, and is INSERT OR IGNORE so a re-observed delivery cannot move an instant and retroactively break reply_confirms_delivered_message. The one trade-off (TeamsInbox single-target evidence is "write landed + wake fired", not "harness surfaced it", costing inbox_poll as a recovery path) is argued in full at the call site and was flagged to the supervisor.

AC1 mechanism traced with file:line, hypothesis replaced not confirmed. AC2 ack terminal across both transports, 4 new regression tests including the observed shape. AC3 no latency regression — one INSERT OR IGNORE per already-terminal delivery, no selection query touched; cas-store --lib 530 passed/0 failed, cas --lib 3945 passed/0 failed/5 ignored (includes cas-d732/cas-ceae/cas-ef14 delivery suites), queue_and_events 77, factory_inbox+delivery+prompt 241, teams+inbox+message_status+coordination 101. task_title: Nothing advances an epic branch after its children merge to main — decide and implement the advancement policy
close_reason:
Supervisor review complete (ver-a98a2bf6c278, APPROVED, no defects); releasing the PendingSupervisorReview hold. Landed on main as squash e567e76a (PR #398).

Delivered: a successful child close whose delivery is proven on the epic's declared integration branch now advances that epic branch, when and only when the epic is strictly behind and a clean ancestor. The advancement is a non-force push of integration_tip to refs/heads/<epic>, followed by a compare-and-swap local update-ref. A divergent epic is refused with an actionable message and never auto-merged or overwritten — advancing one remains an explicit human decision.

Critically, advancement can never fail a close. Every outcome — ADVANCED, REFUSED, CONCURRENT, LOCAL_ONLY, FAILED_LOCAL, FAILED_REMOTE — is recorded as a CAS_EPIC_ADVANCEMENT_V1 decision note stating "Child close remains valid" plus the supervisor action, and a test is named for that contract. A rejected push re-reads the remote and reports CONCURRENT only when it already contains the integration tip, rather than assuming a race. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and core.hooksPath=/dev/null keep a close from ever hanging on a credential prompt or a stray hook.

The safety question was answered from code, not assumption: factory_epic_status resolves parent_branch from the epic WorkTarget (factory_ops.rs:3798-3839) with a comment warning that using the former epic ref would create a false hard-block; epic close routes through the same collector (close_ops.rs:2097-2110, 10031-10041); and that collector derives per-child state from recorded anchors and content/squash equivalence rather than an "only this epic" diff from the epic tip. The epic branch is a synchronization base by documented design, so absorbing unrelated declared-parent history matches established spawn-time behaviour.

Motivating evidence: the supervisor fast-forwarded this epic branch by hand five times in a single session — 01becf0b→d84fcc86→4b25ec93→c7d36cbe→a0617416→0906e520→e567e76a — once after every child that landed, every one a clean fast-forward that nothing in CAS performed. That manual step is what this removes.

Limitation stated rather than glossed: the running cas serve binary predates this commit, so the advancement does not fire until a release ships it. This close does not mean epic drift has already stopped in practice.</reason>
</invoke>

task_title: Relay pairing requests read-only scopes and the CLI can only narrow them, so Commander observer mode is a one-way street
close_reason:
Landed on main via the epic integration c06a7a17 (PR #403); this lane's own commit was 86fb57d2 on the epic branch.

Delivered: the relay pairing flow now requests all six Commander scopes instead of a read-only three. The security boundary was never the client constant — `authorize_with_relay` displays both requested and granted scopes, calls confirm(), and enforces that any --scopes override is a subset (hub_reverse_pairing.rs:312-314, 373-379, 441-454). The page can only ever request; the operator grants on their own machine and can narrow. The read-only whitelist added no protection on top of that and simply made elevation unreachable, since `cas hub authorize --scopes` may never add a scope — so re-pairing minted another read-only credential forever.

The consent prompt now separates control from discovery rather than listing scopes together: "Read access requested" versus "CONTROL ACCESS REQUESTED", the same split for what will be granted, the Commander origin printed explicitly, and an instruction to verify that origin before approving. Disabled controls now carry a controlDisabledReason naming the remedy instead of being silently greyed out.

Evidence: a six-scope create against the real relay returned 201 echoing pane-input/message-send/pane-interrupt, with the sanitized response kept as a durable artifact; `cas --json hub auth list` confirmed device 913b0ff8 as read-only for https://hub.petrastella.io before the change.

STATED LIMITATION: minting an actual control credential requires a deliberate operator action that has NOT been performed — re-pair from Commander, run `cas hub authorize <code>`, verify the origin and the CONTROL ACCESS lines, then confirm with `cas hub auth list`. That step is operator-performed and is not claimed as demonstrated here. Until the operator does it, they remain in observer mode holding a read-only credential valid to 2026-11-13.</reason>

Observed proof: 6 rendered terminals, 2-miss degraded, 4-miss reconnect and backoff, automatic recovery with canvas identities preserved, and observer→CONTROL without pairing.

TWO CONTRACT DEFECTS IN THIS LANE WERE FOUND BY ANOTHER LANE AND FIXED AT SOURCE HERE, which is the outcome I wanted rather than a consumer-side workaround: ConnectionSnapshot tracked the MACHINE event stream so a Connecting timer would have shown heartbeat age instead of terminal-attach age (fixed with per-session AttachSnapshot); and `since` reset on every transition while stages time out at 3-5s, making the 15s Retry/Diagnose threshold unreachable (fixed with a separate attachSince preserved across the retry lifecycle). A third, latencyMs set to 0 before any measurement, was fixed by omitting the field until measured.

The transport slice consumed cas-f6ab's PaneKeyframe contract unchanged rather than defining a competing keyframe, which is why two lanes worked the same handshake all night with no conflict in it.

Closed centrally by the supervisor; the worker's own close attempts were rejected on worktree-branch reachability after the squash, which is CAS bookkeeping rather than a question about the delivery.</reason>

task_title: Cloud sync silently never registers the project with the team — sync must register or fail loud; team-memories back-fill must work
close_reason:
Both parts delivered and merged (epic tip b6e4bb36 carries factory/calm-condor-85 @ 81033586; part 1 landed earlier as 037a3c0d).

ROOT CAUSE (verified, file:line): project↔team registration existed only as a side effect of a NON-EMPTY team push. cloud/syncer/team_push.rs:28-33 returns SyncResult::default() with zero HTTP calls when `pending_for_team` is empty, and team rows are enqueued only at write time (store/syncing_entry.rs:77, syncing_task.rs:59, syncing_skill.rs:57, syncing.rs:100). A clean install therefore never sent POST /api/teams/{id}/sync/push, the server never learned the project existed, execute_sync still printed both checkmarks and exited 0, and team-memories (cli/cloud.rs:3070-3081) answered with the circular "hasn't been synced yet".

PART 1 — fail loud: new cloud/team_registration.rs verifies with GET /api/teams/{id}/projects, registers via an entity-less push carrying project_canonical_id + git_remote, then re-verifies; only the server listing the project counts as registered. Wired into execute_sync BEFORE execute_push so no green push line can precede an unregistered project; any failure exits non-zero with the real reason plus the exact HTTP interaction. Confirmed registrations cached in sync-queue metadata, re-verified on --full. team-memories message now names project/team/endpoint instead of repeating the command just run. Finding #6 fixed: team show shares team auto's find_team_display resolution (raw-UUID `team set` leaves team_slug None — cli/cloud.rs:735-737).

PART 2 — automatic team default (operator directive; plan approved by supervisor): cloud/config.rs adopt_team_scope_for_configs / maybe_adopt_team_scope. Logged in + no effective team + exactly one resolvable team (user default_team_id, else sole membership) → sync writes team_auto_promote=Some(true) before registration and before execute_push opens the syncing stores. `team set` still wins; `team auto off` is never re-adopted; ≥2 teams with no default gets a "pick one" notice, never a guess; adoption prints the team plus the opt-out, and `team clear` warns the next sync re-adopts. No git-remote gate, per supervisor. cas-f8e3 GUARD REVERSAL RATIONALE recorded in code at the guard itself (config.rs step 1.5): the operator reversed the default, NOT the guard — sync supplies the opt-in explicitly, visibly and reversibly, instead of making the resolver fall through, which would turn team scope into an invisible ambient property for every non-sync caller (stores, MCP, daemon) with no notice, no record, and no anchor for the kill switch.

MERGE-INTERACTION DEFECT caught during epic integration: cas-046d moved credentials to machine-wide ~/.cas/cloud.json; CloudConfig::load() inherits them but load_from_cas_dir (config.rs:1147-1150) does not, so adoption read "not logged in" for exactly the fresh-clone case it exists for — it would have shipped inert. Fixed, unit-tested (adoption_accepts_the_machine_wide_login_of_a_fresh_clone), and the e2e test now starts from a project holding no token of its own. Both lanes were individually green; only the merge surfaced it.

TESTS (scripts/run-scoped-tests.sh / nextest, all on the post-merge combined state): team_registration_test 8/8 PASS; --lib cloud 313/313 PASS; team_pull_wiring 9/9; team_scope_e2e 5/5; active_team_id 3/3; team_default 7/7; team_backfill 8/8; team_memories_e2e 3/3; team_sync 11/11; team_set_slug_resolution 8/8; teams_fetch 7/7; cloud_login_scope 1/1; init_non_project_guard 2/2; --lib store:: 84/84. Clippy: no warnings in the new code. Also closed a latent isolation hole in team_pull_wiring_test's no-team sync test, which read the developer's real ~/.cas/cloud.json and would have flipped to a team project once adoption went live.

OPEN, ESCALATED (AC5): whether POST /api/teams/{teamId}/sync/push registers a project when the payload carries project_canonical_id but no entity rows — unverifiable here (no cloud token on this machine; petra-stella-cloud not checked out). Documented with the exact request/response and the fallback ask in docs/requests/BUG-team-project-registration-requires-nonempty-push.md; supervisor is routing it to the cloud app owner. Either way the silent success is gone: if the server short-circuits, the user gets a loud failure naming that interaction.

No hook, script, or daemon in-repo invokes `cas cloud sync`.

On a hit both platform build jobs skip and the tag only downloads, audits and publishes. The lookup is fail-safe — no run, partial run, expired artifact, API outage, unset inputs all decline and fall back to the unchanged cold path, so the accelerator can never be the reason a release cannot ship. Publication is fail-closed on exactly one complete supply path (adopted AND both builds skipped, or no prebuild AND both builds succeeded), with verify required either way, and it re-extracts and re-audits the exact Linux executable it uploads plus records both sha256 digests. Production (002c8ae4): ContextQuery::has_content() now asks whether the assembled query carries any term, so project identity and git branch count and HybridContextScorer stops early-returning onto the query-blind Basic scorer. Query content comes from three facts Cassy already records — the last captured UserPromptSubmit (<=72h, >=20 chars), the previous session's file list (the Stop hook wiped session_files.json after every turn, so that signal had never existed in the field; the wipe now archives first), and the branch read from .git without a subprocess. In-progress task titles are scoped to the reading agent with project-wide as fallback, closing cas-b06c's cross-lane contamination. The narrower old rule survives as has_focused_content() and still gates the "Related to Current Work" section, so a weak query improves ranking without injecting five more memories. Measured decision: the carried prompt is a fallback, not an addition — stacking it on a live task title halved all_working/seeded_task precision@5 (0.0500 -> 0.0250, distinct 51 -> 35), so it is used only when no task states the topic, which is why both seeded_task rows are byte-identical to baseline.

Harness (37441146, e2372667): three query modes measured separately so a gain cannot be attributed to the wrong mechanism. fresh_session_cold_start (no task, no session files, no prompt row) isolates project/branch identity; fresh_session_carried_prompt is the carry-forward regime; seeded_task unchanged. The seeded prompt row deletes itself on drop, because production reads list_recent(1) with no notion of eval modes and a leftover row would silently seed the next mode.

Final baseline: live_tiers seeded 0.010714/0.009566 d43 unchanged; live_tiers cold start 0.010714/0.009566 d1; live_tiers carried 0.010714/0.009566 d33; all_working seeded 0.050000/0.052126 d51 unchanged; all_working cold start 0.007143/0.007015 d2 hits d1; all_working carried 0.039286/0.037096 d35; Basic control 0.007143/0.005102 d1 unchanged; both ambient rows unchanged to six decimals (acceptance criterion 3). task_title: cas update --all-projects silently skips local projects that are not in known_repos and never migrates the user-level ~/.cas store — 18 projects at schema 236 and ~/.cas at 248 after "N projects refreshed · 0 failed"

Root cause was not the brief's "discovery only enumerates known_repos" — the filesystem scan was structurally dead on every real host. cas-cli/src/cli/update.rs scan_for_projects did `if root.join(".cas").is_dir() { insert; return; }`; every host that has run Cassy has ~/.cas, so scanning $HOME inserted $HOME and returned on the first call, and discover_local_projects then removed $HOME as host state. Net: zero filesystem discovery, ever, so discovery collapsed to the 139 known_repos rows — only ~11 of which are live Petrastella projects, the rest dead /tmp dirs. That is exactly the "16-17 projects refreshed" number. The same early return also hid every project nested under a parent project, and ~/Petrastella/.cas exists, so even a working walk would have stopped at Petrastella and never reached pixel-hive. Measured: 29 dirs under ~/Petrastella have .cas/cas.db vs 11 registered.

FIXED (all in update.rs; four asks all landed):
(1) Registration — serve (mcp/server/runtime.rs:119), the factory daemon (cli/factory/daemon.rs:35) and init already upsert, so update was the gap: every scan-discovered project the sweep refreshes is now register_repo()'d, so discovery converges with no manual step. Added `cas update --register <path>` (ensure_host_schema + register_repo_strict; refuses a dir with no .cas) for projects outside $HOME/CAS_PROJECT_ROOTS or deeper than the bound.
(2) Discovery — both halves of the either/or, split by whether there is anything to migrate. scan_for_projects records a project and keeps descending (MAX_SCAN_DEPTH=8), never entering a .cas/ — load-bearing, since .cas/worktrees/<lane> and .cas/backup/<stamp> both contain a cas.db and are not projects — nor hidden/vendored dirs. discover_local_projects returns ProjectDiscovery{projects, unregistered, skipped_unregistered}: scan-only dirs with a cas.db are refreshed and registered; a .cas with no cas.db is listed as "not refreshed (unregistered): N — run `cas update` inside them or `cas update --register <path>`" and counted in the banner.
(3) User-level store — refresh_user_level_store() runs migrations + builtins against ~/.cas, printed as its own "[OK] user-level store:" line and carried in JSON as user_level_store{store,status}; never counted in project totals.

Backstop: 900s sits above nextest's own per-test kill (slow-timeout 60s x terminate-after 10 = 600s), so inside any suite row nextest still kills and names a genuinely hung test — the raised budget only stops a load-slowed init from failing the row first. task_title: Supervisor panes never wake for ordinary traffic: cas-dab2 gate denies every non-lifecycle row, so worker plans/merge requests/dispatch handoffs are delivered but invisible until the supervisor polls
close_reason:
Supervisor pane wakes are now decided from the sender CAS recorded at enqueue time, and a registered worker's merge request wakes an idle supervisor without a poll.

Delivered on factory/bold-heron-25 tip a3e81f6d, merged to epic/epic-v3-15-5-coordination-follow-ups-duplicate-mes-cas-55aa at c01ce1fa. Four commits: ee4d0dd2 (cherry-pick of true-panther-6's 7f178c0c — verified identical by patch-id, so that branch retires with nothing lost), 07f6361f, ffbc7080, fda51375. Each commit green and each leaves wakes functional; the schema/population half landed before the gate half deliberately, because NULL never wakes and a gate-first landing would have silently killed every wake CAS has today.

WHAT WAS WRONG
1. The reported bug: every non-lifecycle supervisor-addressed row was inbox-only, so the messages whose purpose is to unblock the supervisor waited for a poll (merge request 24346 parked a task in AwaitingMerge; dispatch handoff 24370 blocked a close; an execution plan sat unread while the supervisor sent a status check asking why no plan had arrived).
2. The cas-15f2 bypass, folded in by supervisor ruling 24559: the peer-supervisor allowance sat IN FRONT of cas-3dcb's envelope check and turned on names_a_registered_supervisor(agents, source) — a roster lookup of a caller-settable name. `cas factory message --from "<a real supervisor's name>"` therefore skipped envelope corroboration entirely and obtained a PTY write with arbitrary text. The old unit test modelled the forgery as "the roster said no" and could not see it.

WHAT LANDED
- prompt_queue.origin_agent_id / origin_kind: additive, nullable, written ONLY by CAS's own enqueue path from an already-authenticated caller. QueueOrigin {RegisteredAgent{agent_id}, Daemon, Unattributed}; the agent id is the registry id, not a display name, so role resolution cannot be spoofed by naming someone. No backfill — inventing provenance for rows whose sender was never recorded is the fiction the columns exist to prevent.
- Stamped: MCP coordination message/interrupt and factory clear_context -> RegisteredAgent, taken from the session's registry row and never from display_name, row_source, or get_agent_id()'s literal "unknown" fallback; 11 daemon relay sites -> Daemon. `cas factory message` and bridge POST /message cannot stamp AT ALL — they reach the store through methods that take no origin parameter, so there is no expression in those routes that can produce one. That is enforcement by type system, not a runtime default. Commander/hub is left unstamped deliberately: it has a real authenticated principal, but a device credential is not a registry id and minting one would be the same fiction.
- Gate re-keyed: supervisor_wake_class(sender, supervisor_name, source, prompt). Daemon + a lifecycle/worker-died/spawn/CI/attention envelope; Registered{Supervisor} + not this pane's own echo; Registered{Worker} + a CAS-attached <cas-merge-request>. Unstamped, Unattributed and Unresolvable never wake, whatever the payload says.
- message_status separates wake_not_applicable from wake_declined_by_policy with the reason. One prefix used to cover both a routine chat row and an eligible unblock request the pane refused — opposite facts, and the second hid in a wall of the first.
- Fail-safe: one Daemon-stamped <worker-attention kind="supervisor_unread"> per distinct backlog head, naming the unread count and the oldest sender, emitted from the delivery-stalled scan that previously bounced only to senders. This is how a blocker and a verification handoff reach an idle supervisor, satisfying the acceptance criteria's "or is surfaced by an equivalent unread mechanism" clause.
- Two doc comments corrected where they asserted a property that does not hold (factory_supervisor_overlap::names_a_registered_supervisor, and the gate's copy of the same claim). Both are now marked NOT AN AUTHENTICATION CHECK and retained as display/consistency only.

EVERY ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS MET
- "A merge request … sent by a registered worker to its supervisor wakes the supervisor pane": met by the Registered{Worker} + <cas-merge-request> class.
- "verification handoff, or blocker … or is surfaced by an equivalent unread mechanism": met by the supervisor_unread backlog relay.
- "a message whose `source` string is caller-set and whose sender is not a registered agent still cannot obtain a PTY write": met, and enforced by the type system at the enqueue side as well as by the gate refusing Unstamped/Unattributed/Unresolvable.
- "message_status distinguishes 'wake not applicable' from 'wake declined by policy' with the reason": met by WakeOutcome, persisted as "wake_not_applicable: <reason>" / "wake_declined_by_policy: <reason>".
- "Duplicate delivery is either fixed or explained with the two writers named": explained and fixed. cas-cdf9 measured ONE writer performing two writes — delivery.rs:855 deliver_to_worker (the teams-inbox write, which Claude Code renders as <teammate-message>) and delivery.rs:876 pty_nudge (the same text typed into the pane, appearing as the bare "CAS provenance:" turn). director_events and surface_unseen_for_recipient are both exonerated by receipt evidence. Fixed at b3d834bb, already in this branch's base. I confirmed the two call sites exist as described; I did not re-derive the store measurements.

THE THREE JUDGEMENT CALLS, all ruled ACCEPTED AS DELIVERED by the supervisor (msg 24587)
1. `source` is still READ, but only for the Daemon class, where CAS wrote both the stamp and the source. Caught against an existing test: a Closed-transition lifecycle row carries a real envelope but no `lifecycle-wake:` prefix, so envelope-only would have started waking supervisors for progress FYIs — the exact cas-dab2 noise. It is authority nowhere.
2. Only the CAS-framed merge request wakes. Blockers and verification handoffs are free text, and waking on them means waking on a keyword — the check class this task removed. They are delivered through the unread-backlog relay above. The supervisor took the separate follow-up for CAS-emitted blocker/verification-dispatch envelopes as his own and instructed me not to open it; that is a future enhancement, not residual work from this task.
3. The peer-supervisor class trusts the stamped registry Supervisor role with no envelope requirement, stated out loud in the code rather than left implicit. There is no supervisor-to-supervisor envelope to corroborate against, and requiring one would kill the wake v3.15.4 just shipped.

Also load-bearing, and easy to misread as tidiness: wake-eligible rows are excluded from the unread count, because the summary is itself a lifecycle-wake row and would otherwise become its own backlog head without end. And `supervisor_unread` is registered in BOTH worker-attention parsers — the wake-corroboration check and message_ack's outbox-key bridge — since missing the second acks the durable notification and leaves the prompt relay visible in every later worker_status.

CLAIM DISCIPLINE, verbatim per ruling 24559: this raises the bar from "the caller must know a prefix and a tag grammar" to "the caller must be an authenticated registered agent". It does NOT defend against a local process with write access to .cas/cas.db, which can insert a row with any origin it likes. Local store write access remains the trust boundary. No stronger claim is made.

task_title: Director sends false "worker has closed task X" notification while the task is in_progress / just started
close_reason: Root cause pinned with evidence: filter_director_agents_to_current_session() mutates FactoryApp.director_data in place, epic-scoping it to the currently-tracked epic. All 5 documented repros split cleanly across two concurrently-active epics (cas-604d, cas-6d83), confirming the mechanism. Fix: added FactoryApp.unfiltered_director_data, a canonical never-filtered snapshot that change detection and the TaskCompleted render-time safety net now read from; director_data's TUI-display filtering is unchanged. Two new regression tests reproduce the exact mechanism with the real repro task IDs and prove the fix. Merged into epic/epic-factory-operator-truth-fixes-completion-notif-cas-b646 by supervisor (989ce49 + merge fixup 6c64a20 for a concurrent cas-6506 call site collision); factory suite green on the epic tip (269/269 incl. both cas-dbbe regression tests).

THE FIX IS A ONE-LINE PRIORITY INVERSION, AND IT IS THE RIGHT ONE:
  before: resolve_commit_head(input).or_else(|| extract_commit_hash(stdout))   // HEAD preferred
  after:  extract_commit_hash(stdout).or_else(|| resolve_commit_head(input))   // commit output preferred
The commit's own stdout is the authoritative record of what was created; HEAD is only a proxy that a later command in the same chain can move. The short hash from stdout is then resolved to a full SHA via the new `resolve_git_revision`, and HEAD remains the documented fallback for quiet commits that print no hash — so the previously-covered case is preserved rather than traded away.

AC disposition:
1. Verified first, characterization test committed separately and shown red.

A wrong anchor therefore either lets a zero-commit task close as verified, or falsely blocks an unrelated branch. Combined with cas-54ca (the gate now falls back rather than failing open), the anchor path is only trustworthy if the anchor itself is correct — this task is what makes cas-54ca's evidence worth trusting.</parameter>

task_title: Non-urgent messages to an IDLE Codex worker never start a turn — merge/re-close handshake is dead, supervisor must force-close every task
close_reason:
Merged into main (--no-ff) at fd328c68 and pushed to origin. Supervisor gate on merged main: sanitized RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --no-fail-fast, EXIT=0, 116 result blocks, 0 failures.

ROOT CAUSE, live-measured against real codex 0.146.0 through cas's own Mux/Pane code with no stand-in: Codex's TUI runs a paste-burst detector over unframed input. Pane::inject_prompt wrote the payload as one large unframed burst, so the trailing CR was consumed as the paste terminator instead of read as Enter. The payload was left as an unsubmitted draft in the composer — visible in the captured pane viewport behind the `>` marker — and later messages appended to that same stuck draft. Fix: wrap Codex payloads in explicit ESC[200~/ESC[201~ before the submit CR, gated on a new requires_bracketed_paste_injection capability. Claude and Grok payload bytes are unchanged and unit-pinned.

The worker corrected the supervisor's hypothesis with evidence rather than complying with it. I argued both paths sampled a timing race; probe2 sent the CR at confirmed output quiescence (+375ms, EARLIER than the old blind 500ms settle) and it was still swallowed — deterministic, not a race, so it cannot be tuned or retried around. It also proved the trigger is burst SIZE, not newlines (same payload, newlines replaced by spaces: still swallowed). That single mechanism explains all three field shapes and the whole size corpus (78 B and 758 B submit; 1045/1834/1963/2392/2907 B swallowed), collapsing my "two causes, three shapes" and stale-pane-handle theories into one cause. Shape (c) — the urgent that produced no turn_aborted at all — is a pane already holding a stuck draft: no in-flight turn to abort, and new text silently appends to a draft that never reaches the rollout.

AC1 met (repro on first attempt, exact field signature). AC2 met: 3 consecutive clean runs, 12/12 live assertions, covering 1045 B, the 2907 B field ceiling, a single-line control, and the urgent path. AC3 met, urgent tests untouched and green. AC5/AC6 met — the worker MEASURED before changing cas-893c's test, found the ticket's prediction wrong, kept the assertion, and added codex_recipient_is_never_double_typed_by_the_idle_nudge because nudging Codex would have double-typed into the stuck draft. AC7 met: not a regression, incomplete, and the bash stand-in solely responsible — correction notes added at the exact place the false conclusion was recorded. AC8 met, 3 pre-existing parallel flakes triaged to base with a varying failure set.

AC4 PARTIAL, correctly flagged rather than faked. The confirmed/acked half falls out of the fix. The wake/reaction half cannot be met without changing ObservationStatus, a deliberately single-variant enum documented as "Evidence CAS does not fabricate", and supplying a real observation source. Filed as follow-up work rather than bolting a fabricated signal onto a P0 — the right call, and I am recording it as an accepted partial, not an oversight.

Residual risk stated by the worker and accepted: the fix depends on Codex honoring bracketed paste (verified live on 0.146.0). If a future codex changes that, the live tests fail loudly rather than degrading into silent non-delivery — which is precisely the property the old code lacked.

task_title: Close guard ref resolution: remote staging ref, cross-repo anchor, receipt SHA UX (GH #66, #56, #57)
close_reason:
GH #66 (fixed in code): the merge guard re-measures after its best-effort fetch against BOTH the local target ref and origin/<target> (`rev-list <tip> --not <target> origin/<target>`) — a commit reachable from either is merged, only what is on neither counts — and cas-e74c's task-attributable count gets the same scoping. This is what stops a worktree's never-advanced local ref from reporting nine stranded commits when one is unmerged. Unknowable git state keeps the prior local measurement, so nothing fails open. The remediation text no longer claims a `git fetch` can fix a stale LOCAL branch ref (it cannot — fetch only moves remote-tracking refs, and that advice is what sent workers chasing merges that had already landed); it now names what was measured and hands over a `git merge-base --is-ancestor` check.

GH #56 (fixed in code, one half already existed): the declared-target-repo binding asked for in ask #1 was already implemented — task.deliverables.work_target → resolve_repo_context drives close_project_root and target_branch for every close gate, covered by repo_context's wrong_spawn_repo_is_not_used_for_declared_repo_close_gate. The live defect was the addendum's receipt gap: validation ran only inside gates that happened to need the receipt, so on a cross-repo close no gate fired and a SHA existing only in the other repository entered the audit trail as proof. Any supplied commit_receipt is now resolved against the repository the close is bound to, for every caller and every bypass level, and one that does not resolve there is refused with instructions to declare target_repo/target_branch. Ancestry, diff and work-cycle semantics are unchanged and stay with the existing gates.

GH #57 (VERIFIED, NOT CODED — no change was needed): the receipt path already accepts abbreviations, so the issue describes behavior that was fixed after it was written. Evidence, all in cas-cli/src/mcp/tools/core/task/lifecycle/close_ops.rs: resolve_task_commit_receipt_sha (line 6775) accepts 4..=64 hexadecimal characters and resolves them through `git rev-parse --verify --quiet`, then confirms the object is a commit and that the resolution was an object-ID prefix rather than a ref name — the issue's preferred fix #1; the format rejection (line 6784) reads "receipt format invalid: expected 4 to 64 hexadecimal characters; received N characters" — its fallback fix #2; and two regression tests already pin it, cas77af_valid_short_receipt_resolves_to_full_commit_and_proceeds (15470) and cas77af_unmerged_short_receipt_reports_ancestry_not_format_or_merge_required (15528), the second covering exactly the reported confusion (a short receipt for unmerged work reports ancestry, not a format error or MERGE REQUIRED). This delivery adds receipt_repo_binding_check_accepts_an_unambiguous_abbreviation so the new #56 gate cannot regress abbreviation support. Because no code changed for #57, the commit carries only "Fixes #66" and "Fixes #56"; #57 should be closed as already-fixed citing the above. Its remaining suggestion 3 (supervisor-facing tables printing full SHAs) is cosmetic now that abbreviations resolve and was deliberately left alone.

8 new tests (remote-aware count across merged / partially-merged / no-remote / unknowable git, gate message asserting both the corrected count and the absence of the misleading fetch advice, receipt-absent-from-bound-repo refusal, abbreviation still accepted). cargo test --no-fail-fast: 120 targets green, only the 3 known pre-existing env-race flakes. task_title: Epic regression: director idle-suppression test fails intermittently after signal revalidation (events_tests)
close_reason:
Root cause named and fixed test-first; merged into the epic as 24352f39.

Not the cas-6eab revalidation. The failing assertion fires inside the test's DirectorData load, before any prompt exists — the worker was missing from the snapshot the detector is fed, not pruned from a signal — and every file cas-6eab touched is absent from this test's call graph.

Mechanism: agent visibility is decided by the process-global CAS_FACTORY_SESSION read at two moments. AgentStore::register stamps an agent's factory_session from it; DirectorData::load_with_stores then filters through visible_to_factory_session(env), where Some(session) demands an exact match. A consistent value at both moments is harmless — verified empirically both ways — but a flip BETWEEN the two reads erases every agent registered under the old value. The test pinned nothing, so its outcome depended on what a concurrently scheduled test was doing with that variable: that is the intermittency, and why it never reproduced filtered or in isolation. The mutators were supervisor_push's 8 raw set_var/remove_var sites, which held the shared lock but could not be excluded by a test that took no lock, and which also leaked the variable on unwind.

Fix, test-only: the director tests pin the variable through TestEnvGuard across the register-then-load window, and supervisor_push's 8 sites use the same guard instead of manual save/restore so restoration survives panics. No production behaviour changed — strict same-session visibility is deliberate, and the worker-idle suppression semantics the test guards were never involved. Added a regression test reproducing the flip deterministically.

Proof: full workspace cargo test --no-fail-fast green 3 consecutive runs at fa3919fa — 6074 passed, exit 0, zero failures each — plus 4 consecutive green lib runs. No epic test regressed.

Delivery defect on my side, recorded for the record: the commit also carried 80 stray insta .snap.new artifacts under a doubled cas-cli/cas-cli/ path, which the supervisor removed in epic cleanup commit 5bbd8d1d. Cause: I ran the compiled test binary directly from the workspace root while characterising the flake, which made insta write snapshots relative to the wrong cwd; my pre-commit check used git diff --stat, which shows tracked modifications only and never reveals untracked files, and git add -A then swept them in. Correct check is git status --porcelain before staging.

Reported but deliberately NOT fixed (see task notes): server_registry's shared_server_survives_a_worker_cgroup_kill failed twice in early workspace runs and has not recurred in 10 subsequent runs. Mechanism hypothesis with corroborating evidence but no reproduction, so no change was shipped on it.

task_title: Orphan process GC: gc_report/gc_cleanup cover dead-parent processes and stale port squatters (GH #88)
close_reason:
Orphan process GC delivered test-first; merged into the epic as feb2f6d2.

All three GH #88 classes in one pass via new module cas-cli/src/ui/factory/orphan_gc.rs (pure disposition logic separated from /proc scanning so the whole matrix is unit-testable), wired into factory_gc_report, factory_gc_cleanup and the SessionStart banner.

gc_report: processes section covering (a) processes whose cwd is under .cas/worktrees/* with a dead/adopted parent, (b) dev-server processes on registry-recorded ports whose owning session is gone, (c) registry entries whose process has died. Each row carries its evidence — pid, comm, cwd, parent state, bound ports — and every candidate NOT reaped states why (shared / live owner / no fingerprint / pid reused), because a silently filtered orphan is indistinguishable from one CAS never saw.

gc_cleanup: reaps behind force=true AND explicit dry_run=false (the target-cache double gate, applied here for a stronger reason — this is the only GC that signals processes CAS did not start, and a killed dev server cannot be un-killed). shared-flagged registrations spared per the issue; live sessions and live worker process groups spared; every kill revalidates the /proc start-time fingerprint immediately before signalling so a recycled pid is skipped rather than killed; server reaping routes through server_registry::stop so the recorded pgid is signalled, since killpg on a non-leader kills nothing while reporting success. Registry pids are excluded from the dead-parent class outright — registered servers are deliberately reparented by design and would otherwise all read as orphans. Zombies are skipped rather than promised a kill that cannot work.

Session start: banner naming leftovers and the ports they hold with an adopt-or-kill instruction, instead of the next session inheriting them invisibly and meeting them as EADDRINUSE. Visibility only — it never signals anything, because a session start is not consent to kill.

Key finding, measured before coding rather than assumed: adoption is NOT ppid == 1. A deliberately planted orphan on this host was adopted by systemd --user (pid 3251), not pid 1, because the host runs a child_subreaper. The obvious rule would have shipped a GC reporting "no orphans" forever on every systemd-user and most container hosts while ports stayed squatted — and it would have looked like it worked. A parent counts as gone when it is pid 1, no longer exists, or is an init-like manager directly under pid 1; that clause is deliberately narrow so a developer's editor or cargo test inside a worktree keeps a live parent and is never a candidate.

17 new tests: full pure disposition matrix for both classes, /proc stat parsing with parens inside comm, and planted-orphan end-to-end tests (a shell that backgrounds a child and exits) asserting both directions — the orphan is reported and reaped, a live worker's tracked process group in the same worktree is spared, and a preview kills nothing.

cargo test --workspace: 6073 passed, 0 failed — fully green including the hooks::context and factory_preflight tests that were flaky across this epic (cas-c220 fixed them). No test processes leaked. Only the new file was rustfmt'd; the four pre-existing files touched were already non-fmt-clean at HEAD (verified against HEAD copies), so reformatting would have collided with cas-6419/cas-a5c0 on factory_ops.rs.

task_title: Factory: message transport honesty — ack ≠ seen, nudges grant no turns, both directions need polling (GH #102)
close_reason: Messages no longer strand on a worker the agent registry wrongly calls busy, and an inferred ack is no longer reported as a recipient confirmation. Traced the live incident rather than trusting the issue's wording: prompt_queue row 6744's recipient held NO in-progress task (its own was parked awaiting_merge 2m47s before that message was enqueued), so the current_task veto never fired. The real suppression was agent_signals_look_quiet — an automated worker_git_commit checkpoint 112s before delivery still counted as recent activity (window 120s), and last_heartbeat is daemon-stamped from process liveness, so two signals that track neither turns nor work agreed the worker was busy. The "27 min unacked" figure is also not established: that ack matches the recipient's own outbound row to within 0.45ms, i.e. inferred_from_reply. Shipped: failing the registry's idle test no longer ends the enquiry — the pane and transcript are asked instead (sustained wall-clock silence, clean composer, injection readiness, no outstanding tool call via the same resolve_worker + transcript_has_in_flight_tool_call pair is-wedged uses, with unresolvable transcripts counting as in-flight). The tool-call veto is the safety-critical gate and deliberately tightens the pre-existing cas-893c path, which had no pane condition at all: a worker blocked on an approval dialog is silent indefinitely and looks maximally wakeable, and every injected payload ends in a submit CR that would answer the highlighted option. Silence is wall-clock seconds, not poll ticks (process_prompt_queue polls at 100ms, so a tick count meant 300ms). A vetoed nudge no longer consumes the row — cas-f02b's retry-pending rule now covers any inbox-delivered recipient, so a message whose one-instant pane check failed is retried instead of stranded. Ack provenance (explicit_ack vs inferred_from_reply) is recorded and surfaced as confirmation_source; only an explicit ack is presented as the recipient's own claim; legacy acks report unknown. Deleted before shipping: a first-draft sweep that re-injected unacked messages — two reviewers proved it was dead on any real DB (unacked()'s 20-row window saturated by legacy rows the session filter drops only after the SQL LIMIT), that it bypassed the cas-dab2/cas-f02b corroboration and would have PTY-injected ordinary worker chatter into the supervisor pane, and that its "silent since delivery" invariant was never implemented so it could re-inject already-acted-on instructions. Not duplicated: worker_status unread counts are cas-e728's lane. Tests at the delivery layer plus store-level ack provenance tests; cargo test -p cas --lib 3364 pass, cas-store 429, bins warning-free. Merged to the epic branch as 7261cfad.

Traced the path rather than trusting the issue's lead: assignee changes DO produce a TaskAssigned director event for codex workers and delivery already routes codex to PTY (cas-b68a); the fragility is one level down, in how the wake-up is written — none of it reachable for a Claude-under-teams recipient, whose delivery is a durable inbox file. (3) Pane::inject_prompt's detached submit-CR failure is no longer swallowed; it left payloads unsubmitted in the codex composer while the daemon recorded a delivered wake-up and a busy pane. Two independent reviewers ran (correctness + adversarial refutation); both operative findings fixed in the delivered tip. Honest residual recorded on the task: without runtime logs from cas-46eb/cas-1bdb I cannot prove which of the three loss paths fired in those incidents — the readiness path hardens spawn-window assignments rather than mid-session ones — but all three are real, all three are codex/PTY-only, and the next occurrence is diagnosable from the cas::coordination log (director_prompt_queued / director_prompt_requeued / inject_submit_failed). task_title: Factory: MERGE REQUIRED close rejections never reach the supervisor session (GH #101)
close_reason: A worker close parking as awaiting_merge now produces a supervisor-visible push within the daemon tick. The emit was never missing — park_task_awaiting_merge already pushed AwaitingMerge + CloseRejected through the durable lifecycle outbox into a High-priority prompt_queue row targeted at the supervisor. The signal died at the dispatch layer: target_looks_like_idle_worker excludes the supervisor from the idle PTY nudge by construction, so for a Claude supervisor in teams mode the row was an inbox FILE write that an idle supervisor (no turn boundary) never reads; nothing could create a supervisor turn but an urgent interrupt or a human. Two adjacent silences fixed while verifying: worker_looks_idle disqualified any agent holding an InProgress task, which would have permanently disabled the wake for every supervisor owning its epic; and revalidate_lifecycle_prompt required exact updated_at equality, so any write while a task sat parked dropped the park's own notification pre-transport. 13 dispatch-layer tests (wake fires for an idle supervisor, epic-owning supervisor still wakeable, each pane veto independently blocks, forged source rejected, FYI transitions never wake, worker path unchanged, retry identification, end-to-end enqueue of a wake-eligible row, parked-state currency). cargo test -p cas --lib 3360 pass; cas-types 204; cas-mux 105; bins warning-free. Merged to the epic branch as dfef5726.

task_title: MCP: task action=ready silently caps at 10 — print true total, sort by priority (GH #104)
close_reason: task action=ready is now priority-sorted and honest about truncation. Two independent halves caused the reported incident: the header printed only the shown count (so "Ready tasks (10):" was indistinguishable from a drained queue when 30 were waiting), and TaskSortOptions defaults to TaskSortField::Created/DESC, so newer P2/P3 follow-ups filled the window while thirteen ready P0s sat unseen. Unspecified sort now means priority (P0 first) on this surface; an explicit sort= still wins and the header labels the ordering ACTUALLY applied, so sort=created reads "newest first" rather than claiming priority order. When anything is withheld the header carries the true total ("showing 10 of 30, P0 first") and a footer names the withheld count and the exact call that reveals them; an uncapped list keeps the plain form and gets no footer, so a complete list never looks truncated either. The cap itself is kept deliberately — an unbounded dump is its own failure mode; what is fixed is that it was silent. blocked carried the identical silent cap and creation-order default on the same triage surface and uses the same helpers. Review follow-ups: my first regression test was vacuous (P0s created last, but the old default was newest-first, so they surfaced even with the fix reverted — every priority assertion passed against the bug and only the header string failed); blocked had zero end-to-end coverage; an unparseable sort= fell back to created/desc, handing the incident ordering back with no error; and ties were non-deterministic on the epic path because get_subtasks has no ORDER BY. All four fixed and covered. Tests: the reported shape end-to-end with the fixture inverted so creation order genuinely buries the P0s, the same for blocked, uncapped-list, explicit-sort-wins, unparseable-sort fallback, plus 4 unit tests on the helpers. Green: --test mcp_tools_test 277, -p cas --lib mcp::tools 628, -p cas --lib task 530. Commits 6a204a08 and 3d4dc6f2 carry "Fixes #104"; merged to the v3 epic branch as bdd17995.

task_title: cas_tasks_available: honour or reject sort/sort_order instead of silent no-op (GH #111)
close_reason: cas_tasks_available now honours sort/sort_order instead of silently ignoring them. Both params were in the action's schema and routed from the meta-tool into the handler, which dropped them — an agent asking for a different order got the default back with no error and no way to tell. Honoured rather than rejected: rejecting is the smaller diff, but the params are already advertised and already plumbed, so rejecting would break any caller that reasonably assumed they worked. Semantics are cas-06f9's, not a second dialect: unspecified means priority (P0 first), an explicit field wins, and an unrecognised field means unspecified rather than falling back to creation order — that trap would bite harder here than on ready, since this is the surface an idle worker uses to pick its own next task. The header now names the ordering applied, so honouring the parameter is observable rather than inferred, and the three cas-e163 assertions pinning the old header were updated rather than loosened. One new helper (sort_task_refs) because this handler filters list_ready's output by lease into a Vec<&Task> and sort_tasks would have meant cloning every row about to be printed. Default output is unchanged in practice — list_ready already returns priority-first and the new default re-applies the same key; the only rows that can move are those tied on both priority and created_at, where cas-06f9's id tie-break replaces SQLite plan order. Schema doc updated: sort/sort_order previously read "(for list, ready, blocked)", the agent-visible surface, so an agent had no reason to believe available honoured them. Tests: explicit sort=title with priority and title deliberately disagreeing, default still priority-first, unparseable sort falling back to priority, sort_order=desc alone flipping direction, and sort applied BEFORE truncation. Review found my sort-before-truncate test was vacuous (list_ready returns created_at DESC, so the alphabetically-first task created last was already on top); fixture inverted and verified by mutation that it now fails against a sort-after-truncate regression, and the unparseable-sort fixture was fixed the same way. Second vacuous test in this epic from one assumption — recorded as memory 2026-08-06-8: read the store's ORDER BY and the enum's default_order() before reasoning about what creation order implies, then prove the test by mutating the exact production line it guards. Green: --test mcp_tools_test 285, -p cas --lib mcp::tools 634, -p cas-mcp --lib 68. Commits 3ba95b50 and 5566af1c carry "Fixes #111"; merged to the v3 epic branch as d003ffd9.

task_title: cas_tasks_available: add the #104-style withheld-rows footer (GH #109)
close_reason: cas_tasks_available now names the rows it withheld. Same class as GH #104 on the surface idle workers use to self-serve work: the cap of 20 was applied with an honest total but nothing said the list in front of you had been cut, so a worker could read 20 rows, have no reason to connect the larger total to its own view, and never learn which call reveals the rest. Reuses cas-06f9's truncated_list_footer verbatim so the two surfaces cannot drift in wording; the header keeps its existing "(N total)" form, which was already truthful — changing it would churn a contract for no gain. Rows arrive priority-first from list_ready's ORDER BY and the only later step is the claimed-lease filter, which removes rows without reordering, so the withheld tail is genuinely lower-priority work. Tests: 25 claimable tasks under the default cap (honest total survives, withheld count named, footer gives the exact call), a 3-task list asserting no footer when nothing is withheld, an explicit limit=5 case (guards a regression that hardcodes the cap and ignores req.limit, which would otherwise leave the footer's own advice a lie while the suite stayed green), and a claimed-lease case proving the total the footer arithmetic depends on is post-claim (5 of 25 held elsewhere renders "(20 total)"). Footer non-vacuity verified by removing the push and watching the test fail. Review verdict was clean; it independently confirmed limit is reachable and unclamped through task action=available, totals are post-filter, limit>total / limit=0 / empty-list all behave, and nothing in the repo parses "Available Tasks (N total)". Green: --test mcp_tools_test 281, -p cas --lib mcp::tools 628. Commits ce215c05 and eb61a6db carry "Fixes #109"; merged to the v3 epic branch as 62450874.

task_title: Factory: worker_status shows closed tasks as in-progress and cries STALLED at healthy turn-based workers (GH #105)
close_reason: worker_status now reports task state and silence honestly. (1) Stale attribution: leases outlive close and any lease counted as in-progress work, so a finished worker read as busy for the lease duration (default 30m) and drew "⚠ STALLED ... while task in progress" with nothing assigned. Leases now only corroborate a task that is still unfinished, checked against render-time lists. (2) The stall heuristic assumed continuous execution: a heartbeating worker on a harness with no turn-start artifact reports "between turns since <t>" plus its unread-inbox count instead of STALLED. The alarm is narrowed, not removed, and no longer keyed on the heartbeat — last_heartbeat is stamped by the daemon from process liveness, not turn execution, so a Claude worker wedged with its process alive heartbeats forever. It now fires on evidence that survives a wedge: mail unconsumed past the stall threshold with no activity renders "⚠ NOT WAKING" with what to check. Codex/Grok keep the STALLED verdict verbatim.
