task_title: Build: concurrent worker builds OOM-kill rustc (unconditional jobs=16); kills present as hangs; orphan rustc wedges next build (GH #107)
close_reason:
Fixed the orphan-wedge half of GH #107 and corrected the two premises of that issue that were false — I filed them myself off cas-3dc1 and verified them before building on them. Merged to the epic branch as 4891fc86.

WHAT WAS FALSE (evidence, not opinion)
- "workers inherit unconditional jobs=16": no. cas-0bf4 already exports CARGO_BUILD_JOBS for role=worker (crates/cas-pty/src/pty.rs push_worker_cargo_env) and cargo env outranks .cargo/config.toml. My own worker env read CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8; the host is 32 cores, not 16.
- "concurrent builds OOM-kill rustc": no. /proc/vmstat reports oom_kill 0 — the kernel has OOM-killed nothing in the entire session. Every `signal: 9, SIGKILL` in those logs was my own kill -9/pkill. Peak rustc RSS on a scoped build: p100 0.43 GB, median 0.17 GB.
- "kills present as hangs": no. Cargo prints `could not compile X (signal: 9, SIGKILL: kill)` and exits non-zero. The genuine failure mode is a LIVE wedged process, which needs a different response.

DELIVERABLE 1 — jobs derate: tuned, not introduced. The divisor was a hardcoded assumption of 4 workers; Mux::worker_count() is authoritative at spawn, so build_worker_config now derates against the real fleet with the old assumption kept as a FLOOR (max(4, observed)) — a lone worker must not claim cores/1, and fleets <=4 are bit-identical to before. Applied via PtyConfig::apply_worker_build_concurrency (retain-then-push, so no duplicate env entry whose winner would depend on CommandBuilder iteration order). Explicit CAS_FACTORY_CARGO_BUILD_JOBS still short-circuits. Known limitation stated in the doc comment: the value is baked into the child env at spawn, so an early worker keeps its allocation as the fleet grows — the floor is what keeps that harmless.

DELIVERABLE 2 — orphan rustc in gc_report: the substantive fix. worktree_process_disposition spared anything adopted that shared a pgid with a live worker, so an orphaned rustc was reported "spared (live owner)" — which reads as "something owns this" when nothing does. One survived 57 minutes and blocked a later build in a different CARGO_TARGET_DIR. rustc/rustdoc whose parent is reaped are now Reapable regardless of pgid, annotated "build tool with no parent to report to"; gc_cleanup clears them. Safety unchanged: parent.is_adopted() still gates candidacy so a running build is never a candidate, unverifiable pids still RefusedUnverifiable, /proc start-time fingerprint still revalidated immediately before any signal.

DELIVERABLE 3 — SIGKILL vs hang: no code, by finding, and said so on the issue. Cargo already surfaces kills. Documented the diagnosis recipe in cas-worker/references/recovery.md for all three harnesses: read the log for signal:9 first; if absent compare TIME vs ETIME (~0 CPU with large elapsed = wedged and it never recovers); confirm with oom_kill before ever claiming memory exhaustion; and never select build tools by name.

CODE REVIEW — cas-code-review's Codex personas are out of OpenAI credits through Aug 8, so the workflow returns 0 personas_run with residual=[] (an envelope that looks like a clean review but is not one; now tracked as GH #108 / cas-acf83). Substituted Claude-native adversarial reviewers, two rounds. Three HIGH findings, all mine, all fixed in the delivered tip:
1. `cargo` did not belong in BUILD_TOOL_COMMS. Its launcher shell exits BY DESIGN for `cargo build &`/nohup/setsid, so an adopted cargo is routinely a LIVE build; the reviewer found a live counterexample running on this host mid-review (cargo test adopted by systemd --user, cwd in a worktree) that my draft classified Reapable. Removed; rustc/rustdoc keep the override because cargo is the only thing that spawns them, and the #107 incident was an orphaned rustc so nothing is lost. Pinned by a regression test verified non-vacuous (re-adding "cargo" fails it).
2. My own new worker guidance told a wedged worker to run gc_cleanup force=true dry_run=false two lines after warning that name-based kills destroy other workers' builds — and that sweep is NOT worktree-scoped, it reaches every worker since all share a uid. Rewritten: reporting is the worker's, cleanup is the supervisor's, and the fingerprint proves identity, not that the process is unwanted.
3. I had broken the workspace build — `cargo check -p cas --all-targets` does not reach cas-mux's own integration tests, so Pane::worker was called with 14 of 15 args in codex_trust_pre_spawn.rs. Fixed and re-verified with `cargo check --workspace --all-targets`.
Plus 3 LOW: preview over-count in build_add_worker_config when the pane already exists; stale doc still listing cargo; drop guard now also reaps the decoy shell's sleep grandchild via /proc/<pid>/task/<pid>/children rather than killpg (a background job from `sh -c` is not a group leader, so its pgid is the test runner's own group and killpg would SIGKILL cargo).

TESTS: 11 new (5 derate, 5 disposition/detection incl. the cargo-exclusion guard, 1 planted-orphan end-to-end proving a rustc-named orphan in a live worker's group is now reaped, with its counterpart that a non-build-tool in the same position is still spared). GREEN: cas --lib 3355, cas-pty --lib 105, cas-mux --lib 105, cas-mux --test codex_trust_pre_spawn 1, cargo check --workspace --all-targets clean.

DISCLOSURE: while building the test I ran `pgrep -x rustc | tail -1` + kill -9 and killed worker subtle-gopher-97's real in-flight compile of crate cas. Nothing corrupted, they need only re-run, and both team-lead and the supervisor were told immediately so they would not diagnose a phantom. It is the same class of error as the original misdiagnosis and is exactly why the shipped fix keys on parent-reaped plus a fingerprint rather than on process name; the docs now forbid name-based selection explicitly.

task_title: Epic stacking: detect and surface chained epic branches (C on B on A) at creation and in epic_status (GH #110)

task_title: Factory: circular authorization deadlocks post-close standalone fixes — merge needs lease, lease needs assignment, assignment blocked by behindness the merge would fix (GH #106)
close_reason: Circular authorization deadlock resolved (GH #106). Root cause is a measurement bug, not a policy problem: `git rev-list --count HEAD..<epic>` counts the merge node created when the supervisor lands the worker's own lane, so the worker reads as "1 commit behind epic", assignment is refused for staleness, and that refused assignment was the prerequisite worktree_merge asked for. Behindness is now "commits whose content I lack": tree equality first (immune to landing style), then `rev-list --count --no-merges --cherry-pick --right-only HEAD...<ref>`. Measured on fixtures, not reasoned: own lane merged 1→0; own lane squash-merged 1→0; own lane replayed under new SHAs alongside one real epic commit 2→1; another worker's two commits 4→2 unchanged; plain unsynced worker unchanged; squash of another worker's lane still counted. Applied to both consumers: the MCP assignment gate and the `cas factory sync` STALE WORKTREE advisory, which had been telling workers they were behind their own landed work. The other two exits were evaluated and rejected with evidence: allow_behind leaves the measurement wrong so the gate keeps firing on correct state and each recurrence needs a human with a flag; lease-free worktree_merge weakens cas-bd5f (a caller could pair worker A with task B and redirect A's branch into a foreign epic) and is unnecessary because rule 2 of authorize_explicit_task_for_system_b_worker already authorizes on assignee match with no lease — the sanctioned path the deadlock was hiding, previously untested anywhere, now pinned by three tests. Review caught a P0: `git merge --squash` collapses a lane into one commit whose patch-id matches none of the originals, so the commit-level rules alone still counted it and the deadlock returned verbatim for that landing style (close_ops fixtures use --squash); tree equality closes it. Scope boundary documented rather than claimed away: the lease-free merge holds for a task with a parent epic; a standalone task additionally requires allow_trunk=true, which resolve_system_b_merge_target enforces by design and merge_target_remediation already documents. Tests: 6 unit on the measure, 3 on merge authorization, 2 end-to-end through the real assignment gate reproducing the deadlock and its negative control; the deadlock test verified non-vacuous (fails against the naive measure). Peer rows sharing an id but not a title are never treated as replicas; they are reported in their own section precisely to warn a human off `DELETE ... HOW "FOREIGN" IS DECIDED (the part GH #133 left open). Local task rows carry no project column, so attribution uses LOCAL-ACTIVITY EVIDENCE: task_leases, task_lease_history, verifications, verification_dispatches, worker_completion_receipts, worktrees, spawn_queue, loops, worker_delivery_transactions. None of those tables is in the cloud sync payload (entries/tasks/rules/skills/specs/events/prompts/file_changes/commit_links), so a pulled replica arrives without any of them. Verified empirically before relying on it: 1071/1484 cas-src rows carry such evidence, ZERO of the 130 rows shared with ozer do, and 75 of the 128 shared with Accounting have Accounting-side evidence. The evidence is asymmetric — its presence proves nativeness, its absence proves nothing — so a row is called foreign ONLY when this DB has no evidence for it and some peer DB does. Replicas with no evidence anywhere are reported as unattributed ("home unknown"), never accused; rows worked here are native even when peers also hold them (318 of those here).

DELIBERATELY REJECTED: the dependency-orphan fingerprint. A genuine standalone task is a dependency orphan too, so for a REPORT it manufactures false positives on exactly the rows that matter. (It is sound in cas-156b's start advisory only because four further vetoes back it.)

A peer DB that exists but will not open is collected with project, path and error, named in the output, and downgrades the row to Warning even when everything readable was clean. A wholly failed scan renders as a named SKIP carrying the error. The zero case states its own coverage — "0 foreign task row(s): N local row(s) compared against M project DB(s) on (id,title), K DB(s) unreadable" — and a scan with no peers says "nothing was checked for contamination" rather than claiming health. The cost is bounded, read-only, network-free, and degrades safely (no peers => one honest line; markdown store => skipped; failure => named SKIP). `--foreign-rows` gates only the per-row listing, which would otherwise drown the other 15 doctor checks.

task_title: clear_context performs a real context reset for Claude workers — or fails loudly with a verifiable post-condition (GH #145)
close_reason:
clear_context now performs a real, verified context reset for Claude workers, or fails loudly. Merged: factory/rapid-dragon-50 tip 37a91423 landed on epic/github-issue-burn-down-v7-factory-ergonomics-gate--cas-7535 as 2a0c63e6.

ROOT CAUSE: the tool enqueued the literal text "/clear" as an ordinary prompt_queue message; for a Claude worker under Agent Teams that row routes to the team inbox, so the worker read the STRING "/clear" as a teammate note, acknowledged it, and kept its whole conversation — while the tool reported "Queued". Verified live against claude 2.1.224 on a real PTY BEFORE designing anything: typing /clear + CR executes the real slash command, and Claude Code answers by starting a NEW session whose transcript head carries a literal `<command-name>/clear</command-name>` record. That measurement drives the whole design.

FIX: the reset is now a CONTROL command with its own sentinel payload (never readable text) which the daemon matches ahead of all message routing and delivers by typing the recipient harness's own reset command over the interrupt-and-inject PTY channel — it can no longer reach an inbox. clear_context pre-flights every recipient (Codex/Grok are refused up front with nothing queued, because no in-place reset command has been MEASURED for them), waits for the post-condition, and returns old→new session ids plus the evidence path. Unconfirmed, unsupported, or unlocatable ⇒ McpError naming exactly what was and was not observed. AC4: a confirmed reset records the new session id on agent.cc_session_id — the exact key worker_status/worker_activity/is-wedged resolve transcripts by — so the session signature changes and the context band recomputes from the new transcript; the agent-register upsert now COALESCEs cc_session_id so a re-registration cannot erase it.

TESTS (all green, scoped): cas lib factory_context_reset 5/5; cas lib delivery+queue_and_events 140/140; factory_mcp_ops_test 123 passed / 0 failed (4 new: literal-"/clear" shape pinned dead, confirmed reset end-to-end incl. the cc_session_id follow-through, unsupported harness queues nothing, all_workers fans out); cas-store green for the COALESCE change; plus one #[ignore]d live test that drives the PRODUCTION helpers against a real `claude` so the harness claim stays measured, not assumed.

ON GH #145's TWO RESPAWN ESCALATIONS (for the issue's close comment — stated as a hypothesis, not a finding, because I did not reproduce them): part of the reporter's experience is plausibly an OBSERVABILITY ARTIFACT of the staleness this task fixes. CAS resolves a worker's transcript by `agent.cc_session_id ?? agent.id`, so any divergence between the live Claude session and the id CAS holds makes worker_status's session id AND its context/headroom band describe a file that is not the worker's live conversation — which is exactly why "worker_status showed a NEW session id" was not the freshness evidence it appeared to be. What that hypothesis does NOT explain is the workers' own reports of remembering their prior tool calls and commits: that is a genuine continuity signal and points at the spawn path rather than at reporting. Concretely, the Claude spawn passes `--session-id <id>` (crates/cas-pty/src/pty.rs:546-550); if a respawn can reuse an id whose transcript already exists on disk, a genuinely new process would load the prior conversation, matching the reporter's "process-verified respawn was not fresh" and the per-name inconsistency they observed across lanes. I did NOT verify that mechanism (out of scope here, and the brief's constraint barred live spawn/shutdown experiments against real workers), so it should be filed as its own task: prove or disprove session-id/transcript reuse in the spawn path, and give spawn_workers an explicit fresh-context guarantee. Supervisors now have at least one mechanism that is verified end to end — clear_context — and it can no longer lie about having worked.

task_title: daemon.sock role converges onto a live current-binary serve: bounded re-election after owner death + staleness handover after binary replace (GH #163)

AC4: cargo test -p cas --lib mcp:: = 774 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored; 7 new unit tests cover bind refusal, stale-socket-file reclaim, delete/replace/"(deleted)" detection, owner-death takeover verified end-to-end with a real Ping→Pong through the new owner, stale-binary handover, and a 5-way concurrent election resolving to exactly one owner; rustfmt clean on socket.rs. Hook wire-shape audit re-grounded on CAPTURED LIVE PAYLOADS. That mandate found a SECOND dead handler of the GH #165 class, plus the missing Stop loop brake. All four ACs met.

AC1 — TABLE with per-row evidence, committed at docs/analysis/2026-08-07-hook-wire-shape-audit.md (rev 2). Every row is marked WIRE (observed in a capture) or DOC (documented only, not observed), because "documented" and "verified" are not the same claim and conflating them is what caused GH #165.

Method: an isolated Claude config dir at /tmp/wirecap holding only a capture hook (a script appending stdin to payloads.jsonl) registered for all 15 events — no CAS hooks, no MCP servers — then two headless `claude -p` turns in a scratch cwd. Claude Code 2.1.224. The running fleet was never touched and no `cas hook` ran during capture; the copied credentials were deleted afterwards. Captured: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, MessageDisplay, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, SessionEnd. The recipe is written into the doc so it can be re-run.

The captured-wire mandate was vindicated: the capture CONTRADICTED the docs.

FINDING A (new, the headline) — MessageDisplay does not send `message`. Real payload keys: session_id, transcript_path, cwd, prompt_id, hook_event_name, turn_id, message_id, index, final, delta. The assistant text arrives under `delta`, as a stream chunk. So `input.message` was None on every real event and handle_message_display returned at message_display.rs:39-42 every time — the cas-97ba React-Ink crash guard and secret redaction were unreachable in production. Same failure shape as GH #165, hidden the same way: all four of its tests built HookInput by struct literal.
SEVERITY BOUNDED: the guard is default-off behind [hooks] message_display_guard, so nothing regressed for users. The true claim is that the feature could never have worked if switched on. A dead feature, not an incident.

FINDING 1 — stop_hook_active confirmed on the wire (present on both Stop and SubagentStop, false in both captures), declared and read nowhere while CAS blocks Stop in five places. Now declared, read through stop_hook_is_reentrant(), and honoured at ALL FIVE sites. The predecessor's open design question, answered: all five, because the four maintenance blockers ask the agent to spawn a subagent and the condition is unchanged at the next Stop if it declines — exactly the non-self-clearing class the brake exists for — and an open task does not close itself either. handle_loop_iteration (stop_flow.rs:58) is deliberately NOT gated: it also returns a block, but re-blocking is the entire point of `cas loop` and it is bounded by max_iterations; gating it would break the feature rather than protect it.
STILL NO REPRODUCED LOOP. This wires the documented brake. It must not be reported as an observed loop.

FINDING 3 — resolved against the wire: subagent_type corresponds to NO wire key (SubagentStart/Stop send agent_id + agent_type). Same for subagent_prompt — SubagentStart sends no prompt field at all, which independently re-confirms cas-78d3's alias move cost nothing. Both documented as dead-on-arrival and pinned by a test rather than deleted; deletion would churn a large number of unrelated struct literals across cas-cli/src/mcp/** for no behavioural gain, which the scope forbids. Note the `subagent_type` that DOES exist is a member of the Task tool's tool_input object — a different thing entirely.

FINDING 2 — PreCompact trigger/custom_instructions: noted in the table as a capability gap, no code change, per the ruling.

AC2 — both mismatches fixed with captured-wire regression tests. crates/cas-core/src/hooks/types.rs: `delta` aliased onto `message` (Notification really does use `message`, so the alias is additive and a test pins that it still works); `final`→message_is_final and `index` declared; stop_hook_active declared (+alias stopHookActive). Two accessors added so each decision has one home, the cas-78d3 pattern: stop_hook_is_reentrant() and display_text(). display_text() also declines a NON-FINAL chunk — a real consequence of the wire shape, not gold-plating, since both transforms reason over a whole message and a fence or secret split across a chunk boundary cannot be judged from one chunk. Absent `final` is treated as final so a harness that omits it is not silently skipped.
NOT VERIFIED, NOT CLAIMED: headless capture only produced single-chunk messages (index 0, final true). Multi-chunk streaming — in particular whether the renderer applies updatedMessage per chunk — was not observed. The final-chunk gate is the conservative reading and the doc says so.

AC3 — rule-172 created (project scope, paths crates/cas-core/src/hooks/**, cas-cli/src/hooks/**, cas-cli/tests/hook_schema.rs): hook-payload tests must parse raw wire-shape JSON; fixtures must come from a CAPTURED payload, never from docs and never read off CAS's own structs; struct literals allowed only for handler-logic tests once the contract is pinned by a parse test. Without that guard assertion the "does not block" case would pass for the wrong reason if the blocker never fired at all — the same trap cas-3dcb reported hitting.

task_title: Clean-tree receipt guard (cas-40c9) false-alarms on merge-then-close: accept the supervisor's merge commit as valid delivery evidence
close_reason:
Clean-tree receipt guard now recognises a supervisor merge commit as delivery evidence. Delivery: 23c8390e on factory/steady-falcon-66, rebased onto origin/main (one commit, zero epic contamination) and merged to main as b026b80d. Single file: cas-cli/src/mcp/tools/core/task/lifecycle/close_ops.rs (+359/-1).

ROOT CAUSE: CleanTreeReceipt::discrepancy_note() modelled exactly two outcomes — the receipt is the worker's worktree HEAD (fine), or it is a divergence (named). The sanctioned merge-then-close cycle is a third thing and it is the GOOD one: after MERGE REQUIRED the supervisor merges the factory branch, the worker re-closes with the merge SHA, and that SHA can never equal the worker's HEAD by construction. So the guard fired on every correct merge-then-close.

FIX: new ReceiptProvenance enum + classify_commit_receipt(worktree, head, claimed, target_branch), called from the close path using the already-in-scope resolved_parent_branch. MergeOfWorkerTip requires BOTH (a) the receipt resolves in the worker's own object DB AND contains their HEAD as an ancestor, and (b) it is integrated — reachable from target_branch or origin/<target_branch>, else has >=2 parents. Containment is load-bearing: a receipt not carrying the worker's tip cannot be that worker's delivery, which is the misattributed-diff case the guard exists for. Unresolvable receipts fall through to Unknown, so the check FAILS CLOSED — an unverifiable claim is never upgraded to evidence. discrepancy_note() kept as a 1-arg delegate so every existing cas-40c9 test is untouched; the new variant suppresses only the HEAD-mismatch clause. A positive "CLEAN-TREE RECEIPT: MERGE EVIDENCE (cas-8aba)" note is recorded instead of silence, so the trail states WHY head != receipt.

AC(1) MET — merge_receipt_carrying_worker_tip_is_evidence_not_discrepancy: a --no-ff supervisor merge whose second parent is the worker's tip yields no discrepancy note plus the positive merge-evidence note; an abbreviated receipt SHA classifies identically.
AC(2) MET — receipt_not_carrying_worker_tip_still_reports_discrepancy (a real commit not carrying the tip, and an unresolvable all-zeros SHA, both still fire) and receipt_behind_worker_head_keeps_firing (receipt is an ancestor of HEAD, i.e. the worker has later commits the receipt does not cover — still fires).
AC(3) MET, WITH A CORRECTION TO THE TASK PREMISE. The two cited incidents are NOT the same class; verified in git rather than assumed:
  * cas-ab75 (23:27) IS the false alarm — receipt d41d6295 has 2 parents, contains worker tip df4be342, reachable from origin/main => now MergeOfWorkerTip, note suppressed.
  * cas-9d92 (22:00) is a TRUE POSITIVE — receipt 525df53c has 1 parent and does NOT contain that worker's HEAD ac643a18, which was a correction commit made after the merged tip and not yet on main. The worker flagged it themselves ("it is NOT yet on main and needs a second small merge"). The guard was working. It deliberately keeps firing, and receipt_behind_worker_head_keeps_firing pins the shape so a future simplification cannot collapse the two cases.
AC(4) MET — scoped `cargo test --lib -p cas close_ops` on the REBASED base: 305 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (3613 filtered out), covering all 4 new tests plus the pre-existing cas-40c9 clean_tree_receipt_* set. The lone `unused variable: attempt` warning is pre-existing and not in this diff.

This close is itself the merge-then-close shape (receipt b026b80d is a 2-parent merge on origin/main carrying my tip 23c8390e), so it is the right experiment. But it CANNOT validate the fix: the running binary is cas 2.50.0, built from 9114c1a and installed 2026-08-07T18:55:29Z, while this commit landed at 23:45Z. The daemon is executing pre-fix code, so the OLD discrepancy note is expected to fire on this very close. If it appears below, that is the old binary, not a failure of the fix. close_reason:

Hook wire-shape audit re-grounded on CAPTURED LIVE PAYLOADS. That mandate found a SECOND dead handler of the GH #165 class, plus the missing Stop loop brake. All four ACs met.

AC1 — TABLE with per-row evidence, committed at docs/analysis/2026-08-07-hook-wire-shape-audit.md (rev 2). Every row is marked WIRE (observed in a capture) or DOC (documented only, not observed), because "documented" and "verified" are not the same claim and conflating them is what caused GH #165.

Method: an isolated Claude config dir at /tmp/wirecap holding only a capture hook (a script appending stdin to payloads.jsonl) registered for all 15 events — no CAS hooks, no MCP servers — then two headless `claude -p` turns in a scratch cwd. Claude Code 2.1.224. The running fleet was never touched and no `cas hook` ran during capture; the copied credentials were deleted afterwards. Captured: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, MessageDisplay, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, SessionEnd. The recipe is written into the doc so it can be re-run.

The captured-wire mandate was vindicated: the capture CONTRADICTED the docs.

FINDING A (new, the headline) — MessageDisplay does not send `message`. Real payload keys: session_id, transcript_path, cwd, prompt_id, hook_event_name, turn_id, message_id, index, final, delta. The assistant text arrives under `delta`, as a stream chunk. So `input.message` was None on every real event and handle_message_display returned at message_display.rs:39-42 every time — the cas-97ba React-Ink crash guard and secret redaction were unreachable in production. Same failure shape as GH #165, hidden the same way: all four of its tests built HookInput by struct literal.
SEVERITY BOUNDED: the guard is default-off behind [hooks] message_display_guard, so nothing regressed for users. The true claim is that the feature could never have worked if switched on. A dead feature, not an incident.

FINDING 1 — stop_hook_active confirmed on the wire (present on both Stop and SubagentStop, false in both captures), declared and read nowhere while CAS blocks Stop in five places. Now declared, read through stop_hook_is_reentrant(), and honoured at ALL FIVE sites. The predecessor's open design question, answered: all five, because the four maintenance blockers ask the agent to spawn a subagent and the condition is unchanged at the next Stop if it declines — exactly the non-self-clearing class the brake exists for — and an open task does not close itself either. handle_loop_iteration (stop_flow.rs:58) is deliberately NOT gated: it also returns a block, but re-blocking is the entire point of `cas loop` and it is bounded by max_iterations; gating it would break the feature rather than protect it.
STILL NO REPRODUCED LOOP. This wires the documented brake. It must not be reported as an observed loop.

FINDING 3 — resolved against the wire: subagent_type corresponds to NO wire key (SubagentStart/Stop send agent_id + agent_type). Same for subagent_prompt — SubagentStart sends no prompt field at all, which independently re-confirms cas-78d3's alias move cost nothing. Both documented as dead-on-arrival and pinned by a test rather than deleted; deletion would churn a large number of unrelated struct literals across cas-cli/src/mcp/** for no behavioural gain, which the scope forbids. Note the `subagent_type` that DOES exist is a member of the Task tool's tool_input object — a different thing entirely.

FINDING 2 — PreCompact trigger/custom_instructions: noted in the table as a capability gap, no code change, per the ruling.

AC2 — both mismatches fixed with captured-wire regression tests. crates/cas-core/src/hooks/types.rs: `delta` aliased onto `message` (Notification really does use `message`, so the alias is additive and a test pins that it still works); `final`→message_is_final and `index` declared; stop_hook_active declared (+alias stopHookActive). Two accessors added so each decision has one home, the cas-78d3 pattern: stop_hook_is_reentrant() and display_text(). display_text() also declines a NON-FINAL chunk — a real consequence of the wire shape, not gold-plating, since both transforms reason over a whole message and a fence or secret split across a chunk boundary cannot be judged from one chunk. Absent `final` is treated as final so a harness that omits it is not silently skipped.
NOT VERIFIED, NOT CLAIMED: headless capture only produced single-chunk messages (index 0, final true). Multi-chunk streaming — in particular whether the renderer applies updatedMessage per chunk — was not observed. The final-chunk gate is the conservative reading and the doc says so.

AC3 — rule-172 created (project scope, paths crates/cas-core/src/hooks/**, cas-cli/src/hooks/**, cas-cli/tests/hook_schema.rs): hook-payload tests must parse raw wire-shape JSON; fixtures must come from a CAPTURED payload, never from docs and never read off CAS's own structs; struct literals allowed only for handler-logic tests once the contract is pinned by a parse test. DESIGN POINT worth carrying forward: I did NOT replace the Delivered stamp with a Confirmed one, which is the obvious one-line version of this fix and is wrong. atomic_stage_stamp_in_tx keys stamp_transport — and therefore transport_delivered_at, processed_at, and the cas-ac7e prompt_queue_recipient_transport receipt — off `next == DeliveryStage::Delivered`. A lone Confirmed stamp silently drops all three, and dropping processed_at is precisely the cas-d047 (GH #70) failure where a later daemon tick re-writes the row to the inbox and re-types it into an idle pane. So a cosmetic fix would have become a redelivery bug. The MCP inbox_poll resolved only the registered pane name (resolve_inbox_recipient, message.rs) while the turn-start hook resolved both aliases (factory_inbox.rs recipient_aliases). Two consequences: (1) VISIBILITY — rows addressed to `supervisor` were unreachable from the supervisor's own inbox_poll, reachable only via the hook; live measurement 40 of 50 supervisor-addressed rows never receipted (80%) against 15 of 59 for the pane name (25%). (2) REDELIVERY — a row retired under one alias kept no receipt under the other, so the reader that did not write it re-surfaced it on a later turn; the in-turn dedupe in both readers covers only duplicates within one turn. all_workers broadcasts are the sharpest case (exempt from every row-level ack filter, leaving the receipt table as the only thing that can retire one) but were latent in practice — hence "reproduction" for the broadcast half and "measured" for the directed half.

No-op for workers by construction.

task_title: Flake: stash_pop_failure test depends on refs/stash reflog depth — held the v2.69.0 release (GH #388)
close_reason:
Supervisor review complete (ver-1ecc58e44cea, APPROVED); releasing the PendingSupervisorReview hold. Landed on main as squash 40883ff3 (PR #397).

Root cause, concrete rather than "irreducible flake": a 12-character abbreviated SHA is all decimal digits with probability (10/16)^12 ≈ 0.355%, and `git stash` parses an all-decimal revision as a positional reflog index — producing the observed "refs/stash only has 1 entries" and holding the v2.69.0 release. `durable_stash_ref` now appends `^0`, forcing commit-revision parsing while remaining a single shell-safe token, so the recovery instruction keeps naming the stash OBJECT rather than a position. The regression seeds an unrelated prior stash and asserts recovery identifies the object; eight-way concurrency passed 32/32. The comment above the helper explains the hazard so the `^0` is not later deleted as noise.

Bounded generalization audit returned a clean negative result with its method stated: `factory_ops::resolve_stash_ref` is the only production path feeding an abbreviated object ID to a git command with an overloaded numeric/index parser; every other short-SHA helper is a display, receipt, or history diagnostic rather than a revision operand. A negative result with its method recorded means nobody has to re-ask the question.

ONE PROCESS CORRECTION, recorded so it is not repeated: the audit receipt was written inside the disposable worktree (.cas/worktrees/sturdy-crane-16/.cas/artifacts/cas-a819/) rather than the durable artifacts root, so the evidence this close reason cites would have been destroyed at worktree cleanup. task_title: Nothing advances an epic branch after its children merge to main — decide and implement the advancement policy
close_reason:
Supervisor review complete (ver-a98a2bf6c278, APPROVED, no defects); releasing the PendingSupervisorReview hold. Landed on main as squash e567e76a (PR #398).

Delivered: a successful child close whose delivery is proven on the epic's declared integration branch now advances that epic branch, when and only when the epic is strictly behind and a clean ancestor. The advancement is a non-force push of integration_tip to refs/heads/<epic>, followed by a compare-and-swap local update-ref. A divergent epic is refused with an actionable message and never auto-merged or overwritten — advancing one remains an explicit human decision.

Critically, advancement can never fail a close. Every outcome — ADVANCED, REFUSED, CONCURRENT, LOCAL_ONLY, FAILED_LOCAL, FAILED_REMOTE — is recorded as a CAS_EPIC_ADVANCEMENT_V1 decision note stating "Child close remains valid" plus the supervisor action, and a test is named for that contract. A rejected push re-reads the remote and reports CONCURRENT only when it already contains the integration tip, rather than assuming a race. GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and core.hooksPath=/dev/null keep a close from ever hanging on a credential prompt or a stray hook.

The safety question was answered from code, not assumption: factory_epic_status resolves parent_branch from the epic WorkTarget (factory_ops.rs:3798-3839) with a comment warning that using the former epic ref would create a false hard-block; epic close routes through the same collector (close_ops.rs:2097-2110, 10031-10041); and that collector derives per-child state from recorded anchors and content/squash equivalence rather than an "only this epic" diff from the epic tip. The epic branch is a synchronization base by documented design, so absorbing unrelated declared-parent history matches established spawn-time behaviour.

Motivating evidence: the supervisor fast-forwarded this epic branch by hand five times in a single session — 01becf0b→d84fcc86→4b25ec93→c7d36cbe→a0617416→0906e520→e567e76a — once after every child that landed, every one a clean fast-forward that nothing in CAS performed. That manual step is what this removes.

Limitation stated rather than glossed: the running cas serve binary predates this commit, so the advancement does not fire until a release ships it. This close does not mean epic drift has already stopped in practice.</reason>
</invoke>

task_title: Relay pairing requests read-only scopes and the CLI can only narrow them, so Commander observer mode is a one-way street
close_reason:
Landed on main via the epic integration c06a7a17 (PR #403); this lane's own commit was 86fb57d2 on the epic branch.

Delivered: the relay pairing flow now requests all six Commander scopes instead of a read-only three. The security boundary was never the client constant — `authorize_with_relay` displays both requested and granted scopes, calls confirm(), and enforces that any --scopes override is a subset (hub_reverse_pairing.rs:312-314, 373-379, 441-454). The page can only ever request; the operator grants on their own machine and can narrow. The read-only whitelist added no protection on top of that and simply made elevation unreachable, since `cas hub authorize --scopes` may never add a scope — so re-pairing minted another read-only credential forever.

The consent prompt now separates control from discovery rather than listing scopes together: "Read access requested" versus "CONTROL ACCESS REQUESTED", the same split for what will be granted, the Commander origin printed explicitly, and an instruction to verify that origin before approving. Disabled controls now carry a controlDisabledReason naming the remedy instead of being silently greyed out.

Evidence: a six-scope create against the real relay returned 201 echoing pane-input/message-send/pane-interrupt, with the sanitized response kept as a durable artifact; `cas --json hub auth list` confirmed device 913b0ff8 as read-only for https://hub.petrastella.io before the change.

STATED LIMITATION: minting an actual control credential requires a deliberate operator action that has NOT been performed — re-pair from Commander, run `cas hub authorize <code>`, verify the origin and the CONTROL ACCESS lines, then confirm with `cas hub auth list`. That step is operator-performed and is not claimed as demonstrated here. Until the operator does it, they remain in observer mode holding a read-only credential valid to 2026-11-13.</reason>

task_title: Guide §11: connection lifecycle state machine, scope escalation without re-pair, in-UI re-pair, protocol hygiene
close_reason:
Landed on main via epic integration squash b6da4319 (PR #406), one CI run, all green, and verified live on the operator's hub (served bundle a8d648e2, byte-identical to the merged build).

Delivered §11 in full. §11.1: explicit staged lifecycle IDLE → RESOLVING → DIALING → AUTH → ATTACHING → LIVE with per-stage deadlines, FAILED(stage, reason), jittered backoff, heartbeat latency, degraded/reconnect thresholds and scrollback resume. §11.3: pairing establishes a grant ceiling while the session starts at observer, with runtime escalation and no re-pairing — the operator's live complaint. §11.4: expired tokens recover silently while revoked and scope-mismatch surface in-UI re-pair, which previously dead-ended identically. §11.5: proto-2 machine multiplexing at /v1/attach with raw binary PTY frames, resize/events/health channels, versioned handshake and lag-drain to keyframe.

Observed proof: 6 rendered terminals, 2-miss degraded, 4-miss reconnect and backoff, automatic recovery with canvas identities preserved, and observer→CONTROL without pairing.

TWO CONTRACT DEFECTS IN THIS LANE WERE FOUND BY ANOTHER LANE AND FIXED AT SOURCE HERE, which is the outcome I wanted rather than a consumer-side workaround: ConnectionSnapshot tracked the MACHINE event stream so a Connecting timer would have shown heartbeat age instead of terminal-attach age (fixed with per-session AttachSnapshot); and `since` reset on every transition while stages time out at 3-5s, making the 15s Retry/Diagnose threshold unreachable (fixed with a separate attachSince preserved across the retry lifecycle). A third, latencyMs set to 0 before any measurement, was fixed by omitting the field until measured.

The transport slice consumed cas-f6ab's PaneKeyframe contract unchanged rather than defining a competing keyframe, which is why two lanes worked the same handshake all night with no conflict in it.

Closed centrally by the supervisor; the worker's own close attempts were rejected on worktree-branch reachability after the squash, which is CAS bookkeeping rather than a question about the delivery.</reason>
</invoke>

task_title: P0: Commander is still broken for the operator — terminal wraps at the wrong column count, attention cards unmigrated, terminal still will not load
close_reason:
Landed on main via epic integration squash b6da4319 (PR #406), and verified live on the operator's hub.

This task existed because three lanes had shipped, all tests passed, and the operator's verdict on the running build was "still looks like absolute dogshit… still same terminal loading issue." He was right, and I had contributed by verifying with string presence in a served bundle rather than observed behaviour.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND BY CDP CAPTURE, not by reading code: the PTY delivered a 281x65 Welcome while the DOM mount was 379px (~51 cols), and ZERO outbound ResizePane frames were ever sent — main.ts gated ResizePane through canControl(), hub/auth.rs mapped ResizePane to PaneInput, and server.rs additionally required an active lease. A read-only credential could attach but could never tell the PTY its viewport size, so the server rendered 281 columns into a 51-column box. Every stranded edge character and mid-word wrap in the screenshot follows from that. It was never a renderer bug, and the alt-screen fix from cas-9a29 was orthogonal.

Fix separates VIEWPORT GEOMETRY from INPUT AUTHORITY: with no lease held, any pane-read viewer may size; with a lease, only the holder owns shared PTY geometry — so a phone observer cannot reflow a desktop controller's terminal. Observed: 379x778 → 51x48, 278x240 → 37x14, with promote/demote emitting exact reversed sizes.

The second half — terminals that would not connect at all — was traced to the initial Welcome exceeding the 16 MiB WebSocket cap at 44,716,628 bytes and compacted to 210,568 (~212x) with only active panes surviving at a bounded tail, plus hub-side compaction of already-running legacy daemons so the fix applied without restarting sessions. That mechanism was later replaced under cas-f6ab, because a bounded tail is correct in size but invalid as terminal state.

Closed centrally; the worker's close was rejected on worktree reachability after the squash.</reason>
</invoke>

task_title: server_stop reports success while a PTY-wrapped child survives — process-group cleanup escapes through `script -q -c`
close_reason:
Landed on main via epic integration squash b6da4319 (PR #406); the standalone PR #405 was closed as superseded since the commit was folded into the epic to ride one CI run.

ONE ROOT CAUSE, TWO SYMPTOMS, both trust failures where the registry reported a lifecycle state that did not match reality:
1. server_stop returned SUCCESS while a PTY-wrapped child survived. `script` created a PID==PGID==SID PTY child, and private stop was PID-only because the wrapper shared the worker PGID — so it killed and verified only `script` and lost the reparented child.
2. `shared` servers died with their worker despite `shared` promising survival. create_server_scope ran from an MCP process already inside the worker cgroup, so the advertised shared scope was actually nested beneath cas-worker-*, and the recursive worker cgroup.kill killed it. Move-after-fork also let descendants remain behind.

Fix: shared scopes become siblings, private scopes stay children, the launcher moves before fork, and teardown is verified rather than assumed.

OPERATOR IMPACT, which is why this was P1 rather than housekeeping: symptom 2 is what killed the restored Commander hub earlier the same night. The operator experienced it as Commander serving 502s and losing his terminal entirely, and it was the first thing he asked me about. Symptom 1 wasted a worker's time when a stop it had been told succeeded left a factory session running and defeated the dead-daemon condition it was deliberately constructing.

Proof: exact `script -q -c 'cas factory …'` reproduction leaves no wrapper or descendant survivor; committed surface 25/25, MCP boundary 7/7, broader factory 689/689.

Found by rapid-hawk-64 reporting it rather than working around it, and fixed by noble-octopus-51.</reason>

task_title: Epic close guard measures against a stale LOCAL parent ref, so it can still emit a merge instruction for work already on the real integration branch
close_reason:
Landed on main via PR #417 (d5622740).

The gate resolved its parent branch by NAME and read_ref_preferring_local preferred the LOCAL ref, so a checkout whose local main trailed origin/main measured every lane against stale main. Measured, same code and same lane, opposite verdict: against local main (two merges behind) factory/steady-kestrel-84 read ContentAbsent and the guidance OFFERED A MERGE COMMAND; against origin/main the same lane was fully contained and read ContentPresent. A false-positive merge instruction of the class cas-b192 removed, arriving through a different door — loud and non-destructive rather than silent, and pre-existing rather than introduced by that fix, which is why the assignee correctly recommended not bundling it into #416.

FIX: branch_content_direction resolves the target name to BOTH the local ref and origin/<name> and combines the readings, reusing the local-or-remote precedent already used by the squash-content path at close_ops.rs:9945 rather than inventing a third strategy. A target already written as origin/... needs no second reading.

COMBINING RULE, reviewed and endorsed as the judgement call in the change: ContentPresent on EITHER reading wins, since merging is unnecessary under any plausible reading of the target; ContentAbsent requires EVERY reading to agree. A merge instruction therefore needs unanimity, so no single stale ref can resurrect a pointless or destructive merge. The asymmetry is intentional and matches the direction of harm.

The single-ref core survives as branch_content_direction_against_ref deliberately, so the test can pin the DEFECT rather than only assert the cure — a test that proves only that the fix works cannot tell you the bug was ever there.

task_title: Close-time task-attributed diff stat reports another task's commit when one worker delivers two tasks from the same lane
close_reason:
Landed on main via PR #415 (1fcb4692).

The close-time diff stat could describe a DIFFERENT task's commit than the one whose commit_receipt was accepted, so the close's own evidence contradicted its receipt. Observed directly: closing cas-069d with receipt abcdb188 (6 files, 182 insertions) accepted that receipt and then printed cf4a117a — cas-66ee's commit (3 files, 15 insertions) — byte for byte, including a file abcdb188 never touched.

MECHANISM, found by the assignee and better than my reported hypothesis. Two parts: (1) factory_branch_anchor captures HEAD at the moment MERGE REQUIRED parks a task, so on a shared worker lane that anchor can BE a sibling task's commit, and it enters known_commits via task_commit_identity(); (2) the validated commit_receipt was never added to TaskCommitIdentity.known_commits, so attribution fell back to the contaminated anchor while the real receipt could be excluded by clock skew. That explains why cas-069d specifically was hit — it was parked by MERGE REQUIRED while its sibling's commit sat at HEAD. I had guessed attribution resolved against the lane tip; the assignee verified rather than inheriting that and corrected it.

FIX: the receipt filters known_commits by ancestry — anything neither the receipt nor an ancestor of it is dropped, removing the sibling — then the receipt is added. Identity-based range attribution runs against a clean identity.

REVIEW HISTORY WORTH KEEPING: v1 computed receipt^..receipt, which fixed the single-commit case and under-reported multi-commit tasks. Measured against a live counter-example — cas-b192 (3 commits at the time, 712 insertions) would have displayed 67 insertions, 9% of the delivery, hiding the commit that fixed the bug. Rejected via request_changes: the original defect over-reported a sibling's work and v1 under-reported the task's own; both hand a reader a false record, and a loud wrong number beats a quiet one. The acceptance criterion said "exactly the commits attributable to that task" — exactly means neither more nor fewer. The stat was never suppressed or narrowed to pass.

Supervisor verified independently: ran the suite from the branch, 19/19, including both decisive cases — explicit_receipt_excludes_sibling_task_commit_cas_0908 and multicommit_task_receipt_shows_all_commits_cas_0908 (3 commits, receipt = tip, all three shown). Read the ancestry filter at close_ops.rs:8380-8406 directly, and trial-merged onto the post-#414 main to confirm zero conflicts after I had wrongly claimed a conflict existed.

Supervisor errors recorded against this task: I claimed the lane conflicted with cas-b192's when it did not — I miscounted a "changed in both" line from git merge-tree as a conflict marker, and the assignee was right. My hypothesis about the mechanism was also directionally right but wrong in detail; the assignee's is the one in this record.

Note for anyone verifying live: this fix lives in close_ops.rs and is only observable through a restarted cas serve. Every MCP server running at close time predated the merge, so a live close may still show the old attribution until a restart. See memory 2026-08-15-13.</reason>

task_title: Fast release publication — the undelivered half of GH #449: tag-to-published-artifacts in single-digit minutes via self-hosted release builds started at release-PR merge
close_reason:
Delivered AC1, AC2 and AC4 via PR #573 (merged to main 19:44:40Z as 267b42d7; commits 31a3f64c, e3f10495, 6b279798). AC3 and AC5 are deliberately SPLIT OUT to gate task cas-2ce6 and are NOT claimed here.

AC1 — BASELINE MEASURED. Tag push -> published, from the GitHub API: v3.1.0 13m18s, v3.0.0 14m55s, v3.2.0 20m03s, v2.72.0 26m26s, and v3.4.0 15m33s (933s; the last cold-path release, measured live today with the new receipt tool). Mean 18m03s over five releases. The critical path is the two COLD platform builds in every one of them: on v3.4.0, Build macOS ARM64 was 15m13s and Build Linux x86_64 12m09s of a 15m33s release, while Create Release itself took 17 seconds and Verify Release Inputs (4m54s) ran in parallel. macOS ARM64 is the long pole and there is no Mac in the fleet, so a self-hosted Linux speedup alone provably cannot reach the <10 minute target — building at release-PR merge is the only sufficient lever. That finding is what shaped the whole design.

AC2 — ARCHITECTURE IMPLEMENTED. New .github/workflows/release-prebuild.yml builds both shipped artifacts on the release-PR merge to main, behind a cheap gate (scripts/detect-pending-release.sh: every release-train crate on one semver, a CHANGELOG heading for it, and no such tag on origin). The gate is self-disarming once the tag exists, so ordinary main pushes stay cheap. release.yml gained prebuilt-lookup (scripts/find-release-prebuild.sh), which adopts only a successful prebuild run whose head_sha is exactly the tagged commit with both artifacts present and unexpired; commit identity, not tree identity, matching what check-release-preflight.sh already enforces. On a hit both platform build jobs skip and the tag only downloads, audits and publishes. The lookup is fail-safe — no run, partial run, expired artifact, API outage, unset inputs all decline and fall back to the unchanged cold path, so the accelerator can never be the reason a release cannot ship. Publication is fail-closed on exactly one complete supply path (adopted AND both builds skipped, or no prebuild AND both builds succeeded), with verify required either way, and it re-extracts and re-audits the exact Linux executable it uploads plus records both sha256 digests. The codesign gate (cas-67c1) travels with whichever job produces Darwin bytes: both producing jobs re-sign after strip and run `codesign --verify --verbose=4` before packaging, so nothing downstream can publish unsigned bytes.

FIRST LIVE RECEIPT for the load-sensitive half: the #573 merge push itself triggered Release Prebuild (run 32410322395, headSha 267b42d7, success). The gate job ran 7 seconds, logged `pending=false / reason=v3.4.0 already exists on origin`, and every downstream lane skipped. An ordinary main push therefore costs seven seconds of one ubuntu job and opens nothing — no hosted macOS runner, no self-hosted lane, no compilation. The standing CI-load policy is intact and the self-disarming behaviour is confirmed on real data.

AC4 — TRUST POSTURE UNCHANGED, ROUTING PINNED. Self-hosted routing uses ci.yml's two-key pattern: the label is selected BEFORE runner assignment behind opt-in `vars.CASSY_RELEASE_SELF_HOSTED` (left unset per operator instruction, so every lane currently runs hosted exactly as before), then scripts/check-release-runner-trust.sh re-asserts on the machine itself — push event, canonical repository, routing enabled, ref in {refs/heads/main, refs/tags/v*}, CARGO_TARGET_DIR and SCCACHE_DIR isolated under /var/lib/cassy-actions, sccache port 4227, non-root. The only contents:write job is pinned to ubuntu-latest and the contract forbids the box's label from appearing in it. scripts/test-ci-test-tiers.sh keeps all 596 pre-existing assertions and adds a fast-publication section pinning the trigger surface, the pending-release gate, audit and codesign parity between prebuild and fallback, fail-safe lookup, fail-closed publication, both routing keys, and hosted-only publication. Four new self-tests (42 assertions) are wired into `make -C cas-cli test-ci-tiers` so none can go stale unrun.

AC3 and AC5 — OPEN, tracked by cas-2ce6. A sub-600s receipt on a real release, and closing GH #449 on it, require the next version-bump merge to arm the prebuild and then a tag push; the worker pre-push hook forbids workers from pushing tags, so the demonstration is inherently supervisor/operator work. The tooling for it is delivered and already exercised on a real release: scripts/release-latency-receipt.sh measures from the FIRST Release run of the tag so a rerun cannot flatter the number, and on v3.4.0 it correctly exited non-zero with "took 933s from tag push to publication, over the 600s budget". task_title: Phase 4 fix round (index repair): bounded lock acquisition, repair failures must not disable background indexing, snapshot-after-lock, all-or-nothing legacy-root retirement, bounded maintenance-arm hold
close_reason:
All five Phase 4 findings plus the three supervisor-requested additions are delivered and merged. factory/fast-robin-31 commits b5b71d69 (merged at bc6944d9) and 5a1b144c (merged at c24f43c5); both confirmed ancestors of the epic tip.

PROOF at the epic tip: 524 lib tests pass across legacy_index + daemon + doctor + hybrid_search. retrieval_eval_test 26/26 (unaffected). `cargo clippy -p cas --lib --tests` clean on every touched file.

BOTH P1 TESTS WERE VERIFIED RED BEFORE BEING MADE GREEN, by temporarily restoring the pre-fix code and then restoring mine (`git diff` clean before commit):
- a_held_meta_lock_returns_busy_instead_of_hanging: FAILED at 30.021s with "Timeout" against the blocking META_LOCK — it reproduced the production hang exactly. Now returns Busy in 3.0s.
- a_failing_legacy_repair_still_indexes_pending_entries: FAILED with "indexed 0" against the early return. Now the cycle keeps indexing and reports the failure.

THE FIVE FINDINGS.
P1-A bounded lock acquisition: `acquire_lock(&META_LOCK)` was an unbounded blocking flock (tantivy declares META_LOCK `is_blocking: true`), so a pre-fix `cas serve` holding the legacy root hung `doctor --fix` and, through `run_maintenance`, wedged the whole daemon select! loop. Repair now uses a non-blocking twin of the lock with a 3s deadline and returns a typed `LegacyRepairOutcome::Busy`; doctor renders a Warning naming condition and remedy, the daemon skips the cycle.
P1-B repair failure must not disable indexing: `generate_bm25_index` no longer returns early. Repair errors, Busy skips and unswept-file counts all land in `IndexingResult.errors` and the cycle still drains the pending queue.
P2-A snapshot after the lock: order is now probe-meta -> writer-lock -> snapshot -> requeue -> meta-lock -> retire, pinned by a test asserting a contended repair mutates neither the pending queue nor the legacy root.
P2-B recoverable retirement: ids are durably re-queued first, `meta.json` goes first (after which the root can no longer strand anything), per-file removal failures are tolerated and COLLECTED instead of aborting, and `.managed.json` goes last so a partial run leaves exactly the list the next run resumes from. A `sweep_managed_files` path handles "meta.json gone, .managed.json present".
P2-C bounded per-cycle work: `LegacyRepairLimits { batch_size, max_per_run }`; the daemon passes its configured budget, `doctor --fix` passes `unbounded()`.

THE THREE ADDITIONS.
(1) Residual race closed one level up, at BOTH call sites. tantivy 0.25 exposes no timeout on `IndexReader`'s own META_LOCK acquisition, so the inner probe cannot cover the window between probe and `Index::reader()`. `repair_legacy_index_bounded` runs repair on a dedicated thread and abandons it after a wall-clock budget — 20s daemon, 300s doctor. Detached-thread safety is argued rather than assumed: the worker holds no lock of ours, its re-queue is idempotent, retirement takes the writer lock so it cannot race a later attempt, and doctor exiting mid-sweep is safe because ids are re-queued before any delete and `.managed.json` survives.
(2) Coverage at both sites. `doctor_fix_against_a_held_legacy_lock_warns_within_a_bounded_time` (extracted `legacy_index_autofix` to make `--fix` drivable) and `a_held_legacy_lock_does_not_wedge_the_daemon_cycle` — the latter added in 5a1b144c after I re-read the requirement and found I had tested only one site. Plus two wrapper tests: zero budget -> Busy naming "budget", 60s budget -> the real outcome, so the bound cannot silently swallow every repair.
(3) P3 #7 in count-and-report form. `non_entry_documents` / `retired_non_entry_documents` tally by doc type; doctor warns naming exactly what was dropped, the daemon pushes one error row per type, and `requeued_entries` is documented as counting entry IDS not documents. I did NOT auto-reindex those types: `mark_index_pending_batch` is entries-only, so a real re-queue means reaching into the task/rule/skill/spec stores and calling `reindex_all` — supervisor confirmed that stays out of scope and recorded it on cas-c6c7.

P3 #5 taken because it was three lines: retirement removes the `.tantivy-*.lock` files it created, after dropping its own guards. #6 and #8 filed by the supervisor as cas-c6c7 and cas-a6d6.

TWO SELF-INFLICTED DEADLOCKS I HIT AND FIXED, recorded because the trap is subtle and bit twice:
1. Holding META_LOCK across the snapshot read deadlocks the process against itself — `Index::reader()` acquires META_LOCK internally, which is literally its documented purpose, and the lock is blocking. My first implementation hung three tests. Fixed by probing the meta lock (acquire non-blocking, drop immediately) before opening any reader, and holding it only for the deletion phase.
2. The same trap in my own new doctor test, which asserted on `inspect_legacy_index` while still holding the lock and hung >420s. Fixed by dropping the guard before the assertion.
The rule: anything that opens a tantivy `IndexReader` must not run under META_LOCK. It is in the module docs and in both tests' comments; the supervisor saved it as a durable memory.

close_reason:
Decision A executed: `apply_boosts` and the three boost flags are deleted, with the measurement that justifies it committed. Both commits merged by the supervisor into epic/epic-memory-system-effectiveness-program-close-the-cas-8fac — fa8a2140 at 5ecad575a1f7, follow-up 4f33907e at 4f56ab98f8ee (branch CI green on both).

PROOF: `scripts/run-scoped-tests.sh -p cas --test retrieval_eval_test` -> 22 tests run: 22 passed, 0 skipped in 5.259s. `-p cas --lib hybrid_search` -> 113 passed. `cargo clippy -p cas --lib --tests` -> clean on every touched file (the two warnings my own deletion introduced — orphaned `chrono` imports and a stranded doc comment — are fixed; the remaining warnings in those files are pre-existing `unwrap_used` pedantics I did not author).

AC1 — measured table committed at docs/analysis/2026-08-31-cas-e979-ranking-boosts.md: config x precision@5/recall@5 x selector, five boost configs x enable_temporal on/off, across all_working/seeded_task, live_tiers/seeded_task and all_working/fresh_session.

AC2 — deletion, not enablement, with the reason and the numbers. Removed `SearchOptions::{boost_feedback, boost_recency, boost_importance, recency_half_life}`, `SearchIndex::apply_boosts` and its call site, the test-only setter and the module doc example. hybrid.rs:547 deliberately untouched per direction.

AC3 — harness gate green on the final configuration, and the committed baseline is UNCHANGED by the deletion. That is the cleanest available proof the removed code was dead: deleting it did not move a single digit.

AC4 — scoped tests pass (22 + 113 above).

THE FINDING. The boosts were not worse; their output was never read. `SearchIndex::search` wrote the boosted value into `score`/`boosted_score` and left `bm25_score` raw; `HybridSearch::search` — the only production consumer — read `r.bm25_score`, discarding it one line later. The boost-induced reordering was discarded too (results are mapped to (id, score) pairs and re-fused), and `truncate(opts.limit)` could have preserved a membership effect but the production caller passes limit = entries*2, so it never bites. No caller of `SearchIndex::search` exists outside `HybridSearch`, and `search_unified` (the `mcp__cas__search` tool) never called apply_boosts at all. Ten arms x three mode combinations produced ONE distinct result per combination.

That the null is real rather than a wiring failure in my experiment is proven by the temporal control: flipping `enable_temporal` through the same options struct changes the BM25 result set (189 -> 185) and its entire head.

PREMISE CORRECTION I RAISED AND THE SUPERVISOR APPROVED: the decision rule named the ambient selectors, but `ambient_recall.rs` never enters `hybrid_search` (verified by grep), so they can neither regress nor improve — applied literally the rule would have mandated deletion regardless of the evidence. Rule re-scoped onto `helpful_memories_production`; ambient reported as measured invariants that demonstrate the scoping.

CORPUS vs CODE INERTNESS, as requested: `feedback` is CORPUS-limited (4/189 entries have helpful_count>0, ZERO have harmful_count, so the multiplier is ~1.0 for 185/189) with the re-open condition tied to cas-8f93's attribution populating at scale plus a larger fixture; `importance` is CODE-limited (158/189 above 0.5, inert purely from the field read); `recency` is neither — inert alone, but it cancels importance's gain when the temporal channel is on. That interaction is only visible because of the paired enable_temporal runs; a single-config A/B would have reported "all boosts do nothing" and hidden it.

COUNTERFACTUAL, measured then reverted (git diff clean): patching hybrid.rs to read `r.score` makes `importance` worth +7.2% P@5 / +6.9% R@5. I did NOT act on it — that is one case out of 56 flipping, inside re-labeling noise, and the change also shifts the BM25 channel from raw ~30-scale to calibrated 0-1 into fusion. Filed as cas-e7ae and referenced by id in the addendum, framed defect-not-dead-feature with the fusion-input caveat.

HARNESS, per direction: the scorer-swap rig is retained and reusable (cas-3b80, the cas-e7ae fusion decision) but carries NO config for deleted code — `ScorerConfig` holds only `temporal`. `ConfigurableHybridScorer` calls the real `contextual_overlap_bonus` (re-exposed `pub(crate)`) rather than copying it, and `the_scorer_replica_matches_production_under_the_production_config` holds it ranking-identical to the real `HybridContextScorer` on all 56 cases in both query modes. No number from an unpinned replica was ever reported.

ONE HONEST ASYMMETRY I SURFACED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: `enable_temporal` was kept because the channel is real at the search boundary, but its effect does NOT reach the @5 metric on this fixture — build_start's tier filter, the overlap bonus and the high-importance-preference sort dominate the survivors, and the top-5 truncates before the temporal reordering matters. I first wrote a test asserting the arms must differ; it failed, and the honest fix was to assert the equality plus its reason rather than to weaken the claim quietly. So: the boosts were discarded at the field read (never consumed); temporal is consumed but washed out downstream. Different failure modes, and the second is one more reason tier starvation (cas-763b) gates ranking work on the shipped path — on live_tiers no arm moved any metric at all.

task_title: Commander: clicks are eaten when a deferred shell rebuild flushes on focusout between pointerdown and click (cas-8434 regression) — #pair-cancel no longer closes #pair-dialog; Send can be affected too
close_reason:
Cancel closes the pairing dialog on the first tap again, and a deferred rebuild can no longer swallow the click that released it. Delivered on factory/true-wolf-76 as 17cfbbd5, merged into the epic by the supervisor as eb40ffa2.

The filed premise was wrong and I corrected it before fixing anything: this is not pre-existing, it is a regression from cas-8434 (merged as 283ff7db). My original evidence was a flawed probe — smoke.js never clicked #pair-cancel, because the create-code dialog renders #pair-close, so it recorded "dialog still open" for a button it had never pressed. Tracing HTMLDialogElement.prototype.close/showModal with the same script on three trees: a62c0ed0 closes on the first click; the cas-8434 tree produces no close() at all, only a showModal, and stays open; this fix closes on the first click.

Mechanism, established by experiment rather than reading: pointerdown moves focus off the autofocused field, focusout fires, the rebuild deferred by cas-8434 flushes, render() replaces the shell including the button under the finger, and the browser then dispatches the click to a detached node. Blurring the field first absorbs the deferred rebuild and the identical click works end to end — that asymmetry is the proof. Nothing about it is pairing-specific: any control clicked while a text field has focus could lose its click, Send in the supervisor composer included, which is why I raised it to the supervisor as soon as I had the measurement instead of waiting for close.

Fix: DeferredRenderScheduler in src/deferred-render.ts owns the release rule. focusout flushes a deferred rebuild only when no pointer gesture is in flight, and a gesture releases it through a macrotask, which the browser runs after the click. A microtask is not sufficient — the click is dispatched in the same task as the pointerup, and the render invariant now pins that choice along with the pointer listeners.

Verified in Chromium at 412x915, run against both the fixed tree and the broken one so it is a regression check rather than a passing assertion (evidence at /home/pippenz/.cas/artifacts/cas-c142/: README.md, mechanism.js, verify.js, verify/probe.json, verify-broken/probe.json, frames):
- invitation Cancel: broken tree stays open with no close() traced; fixed tree closes with "Pairing cancelled." shown.
- composer Send with a structural rebuild pending and the field still focused: broken tree never reaches the handler and the status stays empty; fixed tree runs the handler and states its reason, with the draft kept. This is the supervisor-requested coverage of the surface cas-8434 set out to protect.
- Escape and create-code Close: close on both trees, so the fix did not narrow anything that already worked.
- After cancel, the re-opened dialog offers the create-code flow and states that a fresh cas hub pair URL is needed.

The pending-invitation rule is decided, documented in DESIGN.md, tested, and signed off by the supervisor: Cancel DISCARDS the invitation. task_title: Factory: a Codex worker whose first turn dies with codex_error_info=unauthorized (revoked refresh token) must be reported FAILED at spawn, not left "assigned, not started" for 34 minutes
close_reason:
A worker killed by its harness account is now reported and its task given back, and the spawn that would create one is refused up front. Commit 1916ed70 on factory/mighty-raven-39, merged to main through the protected queue as PR #694; landed main is 94e7de27, and 1916ed70 is confirmed an ancestor of origin/main from this worktree.

Root cause read from the incident's own rollout rather than inferred: in the Codex rollout for 2026-09-03T14-12-58 each of the two turns is an `event_msg` `task_complete` carrying `last_agent_message: null` and an error whose `codex_error_info` is `unauthorized` and whose message is "Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was revoked. Please log out and sign in again.", at 2428ms and 1234ms. Nothing in the factory read that field, so four workers stayed registered with fresh heartbeats, held their tasks, and produced only a soft "ASSIGNED BUT UNSTARTED — possible missed wake" after 300 seconds. The operator found out 34 minutes later.

The fix has two halves because the failure has two moments.

Before the spawn: `preflight_account_auth` runs in factory_spawn_workers immediately before the request becomes worktrees. For each distinct account a request resolves to — the spec's own config_dir, else the captured requester account — it runs the existing bounded probe through the new `capability::probe_account_auth` (`codex login status`, `claude auth status --json`, the same probes `cas factory doctor` uses) and refuses the spawn naming that account directory and the exact re-login command, stating that no worktree was created and no task assigned. Only an affirmative Unavailable refuses: an absent CLI, a probe that timed out, or a harness with no account plumbing is absence of evidence, and a preflight that failed closed on its own unreliability would ground the factory over a slow binary. The whole preflight is bounded at five seconds and each distinct account is probed once. The pre-existing `preflight_codex_config_dir` is untouched and still proves only that an auth.json file exists — which is exactly what a revoked token defeats.

After it: `relay_auth_failed_workers` runs on the same lifecycle tick as the usage-limit relay, scanning at most every fifteen seconds. On evidence of an account failure it releases the worker's task bindings back to open first — the held task is what blocks the epic, and it must not depend on a relay write succeeding — then records the spawn as failed rather than registered in the spawn audit, and relays one message to the supervisor naming the worker, the harness's own words, the remedy for that specific account, and how many tasks were released. Episodes are deduplicated by agent id plus evidence timestamp so the supervisor is told once per failure rather than once per scan, and a failed relay deliberately leaves the dedupe key unset so the next scan retries instead of losing the report.

The scanners live in a new pure module, cas-cli/src/factory_auth_health.rs, over an AuthFailureEvidence of Failed / Healthy / Unavailable, covering Codex rollouts and Claude transcripts. Two policies are deliberate and tested: latest-terminal-turn-wins, so a transient authorization failure the harness itself retried past cannot kill a working worker, which is the false-positive guard the brief asked for; and Unavailable-is-not-Healthy, so an unreadable transcript can never close an open episode.

Fourteen new tests. Nine over the detectors: the unauthorized first turn with its message and timestamp preserved, a healthy first turn, transient-then-recovered, a turn that failed for an unrelated reason, an empty or unparseable tail reading as Unavailable, Claude OAuth expiry closed by a later assistant answer, and Claude prose mentioning an api key or a 401 that must not be mistaken for a broken account. Four over the preflight policy: a logged-out account refuses while naming the directory and `codex login`, the default account is named as ~/.codex when the caller named none, Unknown and Available both pass, and four specs across three distinct accounts cost exactly three probes with a harness lacking account plumbing never probed. One over the seam: a registered Codex agent with a spawn-time CODEX_HOME reads its own rollout as an account failure. Beyond fixtures, the detector was run against the actual incident rollout on this host through a temporary integration test, which reported the failure with the revoked-token message; that test was removed after the run because it depended on a path outside the repository.

Scoped suites pass: factory_auth_health 9, factory_ops 245, ui::factory 734, capability 7, with the supervisor independently measuring 978 tests in the factory scope in this worktree, and `cargo check -p cas --lib` clean.

task_title: GH #703: post-merge merge-request suppressor compares a stale recorded branch anchor, telling workers unmerged fixes "already landed"

ROOT CAUSE, verified in source and matching the operator report exactly: cas-cli/src/mcp/tools/service/agent_search_system/message.rs selected the tip to revalidate as `task.deliverables.factory_branch_anchor.clone().or_else(|| resolve_branch_sha(&repo.repo_root, &branch))` — the recorded anchor FIRST, the live branch only as a fallback. That anchor is written at the previous merge/close, so after the merge at 2106d99db the worker's later commits 784222514 and 44a46dfc1 were both judged as 2106d99db, which is an ancestor of the target with its content present; revalidate_merge_request (prompt_revalidation.rs) therefore returned AlreadyIntegrated and the request was suppressed with "Merge already landed … Branch tip: 2106d99db" while merge-base --is-ancestor on the live tip said the opposite. Telling a worker that an unmerged fix has shipped is the one direction this check must never fail in.

FIX. New shared `resolve_live_branch_tip` resolves the branch's real position: the remote ref (refs/remotes/origin/<branch>) and the local ref, taking whichever already contains the other. Diverged branches return the published side, so the ancestor and content-presence checks decide from evidence instead of a guess; an unresolvable branch returns None and callers deliver rather than suppress. Suppression still requires the live tip to be an ancestor of the target AND content Present/Superseded, so the cas-b278 dropped-content rule is untouched. The anchor is not discarded but demoted to a reported datum: MergeRequestEnvelope gained an additive `anchor_tip` (serde default, skipped when absent, emitted only when it differs from the live tip). Both revalidation paths — the compose path in message.rs and the queued-delivery path in ui/factory/daemon/runtime/queue_and_events.rs — are driven through the same two helpers, `merge_request_branch` (which branch) and `resolve_live_branch_tip` (which tip), so they cannot drift apart later; the queued path re-resolves at delivery time because a queued request can sit across further pushes, falling back to the envelope tip only when the branch no longer resolves. Guidance already printed the tip it tested, which is now the live one.

The real behaviour is Pending, because revalidate_merge_request resolves the target fine and the ancestor check simply fails for a nonexistent ref. I corrected the test to pin the invariant that actually matters — an unresolvable branch is never reported as AlreadyIntegrated — rather than bending the code to my first guess. The supervisor reviewed and confirmed this is the right invariant.

task_title: coordination shutdown_workers rejects a registered worker by name AND by session id ("Worker target(s) not found") while listing that same worker as known
close_reason:
shutdown_workers target resolution fixed; merged into epic cas-2a89 at 594c3b78 (branch tip 97eecd19).

THE REPORTED SYMPTOM: shutdown_workers rejected an idle worker BY NAME and BY SESSION ID with "Worker target(s) not found", while the same error listed that worker among the known workers.

ROOT CAUSE — three different notions of identity in one handler:
1. The `requested_id` selector matched `worker.id == id || worker.name == id` (name OR id), but the `worker_names` selector matched `worker.name == *name` ONLY. A session id passed through worker_names could therefore never match, while the error printed that id as known. That is the by-session-id half.
2. `worker_names` is typed `Option<String>` — a comma-separated string (crates/cas-mcp/src/types/ops_secondary.rs:561) — and `parse_worker_name_filter` split only on commas. The call was made as `worker_names=["quick-dolphin-15"]`, the JSON array shape the parameter's plural name invites, so the literal bracketed text was compared against the bare name and missed. That is the by-name half.
3. The "Known workers" list in the error was built from a third, scope-filtered set, so a single sentence could assert a target was not found while printing it as known.

WHAT IS NOW TRUE
- One identity definition, `worker_answers_to`: name (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed), agent id, or cc_session_id. Ids are compared exactly, because case-folding opaque tokens invites false positives. It is used by the id selector, the names selector, the missing-target computation, and both of worker_status's filters — the three of them disagreeing was the defect, so identity now has exactly one definition.
- `parse_worker_name_filter` strips brackets and quotes per element, so the documented comma-separated form and the JSON-array form resolve to the same identifiers. Bounded and explicit; nothing beyond those two shapes is guessed.
- The error no longer lies. A target that is registered but outside this session's shutdown scope is reported as REFUSED with the reason; only a genuinely absent target is reported as NOT FOUND. The message can no longer claim both about one target.
- Resolution does not depend on the worker having an assigned task or being non-idle. The task text raised this as a candidate cause; I checked rather than assumed, ruled it out, and pinned it with a test built on an Idle, no-task worker — the reporter's exact state — resolving by name, by agent id, and via the array form.

TESTS: `-E 'test(/^mcp::/)'` 953 passed; `--test mcp_tools_test` 343 passed (factory_ops:: alone 338). Supervisor's gate on this tip: 953 mcp:: lib tests plus mcp_tools_test and factory_mcp_ops_test 500 — all passed. New coverage: identity by name, agent id and session id including case and surrounding whitespace; the JSON-array and comma forms both resolving; an idle no-task worker resolving three ways; an unknown target still resolving to nothing; and an over-correction guard proving a different worker, a truncated id prefix, an empty string and a near-miss name all still fail to resolve — widening identity matching is exactly the kind of fix that can quietly make a destructive action match too much.

VERIFICATION BOUNDARY, stated plainly: I did not execute shutdown_workers to reproduce or confirm. It is destructive and there are live workers on this host, so every behaviour above is pinned at the resolver level rather than through a live MCP round trip. The supervisor reviewed and endorsed that choice.
